Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Let $X$ be a four-dimensional manifold with boundary and let $W$ be a compact surface with boundary. An embedding $e:(W,\partial W)\to(X,\partial X)$ is proper when $e^{-1}(\partial X)=\partial W$. It is locally flat at an interior point of $W$ when there are neighborhoods of the point and its image and a homeomorphism of pairs from those neighborhoods to $(\mathbb R^4,\mathbb R^2)$, with the standard linear plane $\mathbb R^2\subset\mathbb R^4$. It is locally flat at a boundary point when there are such neighborhoods and a homeomorphism of pairs to $(\mathbb R^4_+,\mathbb R^2_+)$, where $\mathbb R^4_+=\{x_4\geq0\}$ and $\mathbb R^2_+=\{x_2=x_3=0,\ x_4\geq0\}$; the line $\partial\mathbb R^2_+$ lies in $\partial\mathbb R^4_+$. A collar of a boundary circle of $W$ is an embedding of that circle times $[0,\varepsilon)$ into $W$ that is the identity on the circle at parameter $0$; a concordance collar is required to agree with the corresponding product collar of the ambient end. A smooth proper surface has the analogous smooth charts and collars, which are also topological locally flat charts.

In ZF, let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be smooth, and let $a\in U$. If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open neighbourhoods $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that $f|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Writing $g=(f|_V)^{-1}$,
$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$
No choice axiom is used.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: **Move a genuine ambient ball by translations.** Choose an interior point $p$ of $F$ and a radius $r>0$ with $|p|+r<1$. The embeddings of the closed radius-$r$ ball $D$ centered at $p$ given by $x\mapsto x-tp$, $0\le t\le1$, stay in the interior of $B^4$: the norm of a point in their image is at most $(1-t)|p|+r<1$. Their compact track has a neighborhood with closure in the interior of $B^4$. By [F1] this isotopy extends ambiently in $\mathbb R^4$ with support in that neighborhood. Its time-one map fixes an ambient neighborhood of the outer boundary, preserves orientation and takes $p$ to $0$, while agreeing with translation on the whole ball $D$. Replace $F$ by its image. No conclusion about any nonround ball complement has been drawn.

**Flatten the surface on an actual neighborhood of zero.** Let $P$ be the tangent plane of the new surface at $0$. Orthogonal projection to $P$ has invertible derivative on that tangent plane, so [F3] writes the surface as $(u,h(u))$ in $P\oplus P^\perp$, with $h(0)=0$ and $Dh(0)=0$. Choose one sufficiently small closed disk in the $u$ coordinates. Its graph is a compact embedded disk in the interior of $B^4$. The maps $u\mapsto(u,(1-t)h(u))$ are an isotopy of that compact disk, since projection to $u$ remains injective with injective differential. Choose the disk small enough that its entire compact track lies in the interior of $B^4$. Apply [F1] again there, obtaining an ambient orientation-preserving diffeomorphism that fixes an ambient neighborhood of the outer boundary and maps the full graph disk to the flat disk. The surface is now exactly $P$ near $0$: the disk interior is an open neighborhood of $0$ within the embedded surface. Its complement outside a smaller such graph disk is compact and misses $0$, so it has positive distance from $0$. Choose $\varepsilon>0$ smaller than that distance and the flat disk radius, and less than $1$. Then the surface meets the actual round ball $B^4_\varepsilon$ precisely in $P\cap B^4_\varepsilon$. Compose the two ambient diffeomorphisms to obtain $\Psi$. They fix a common ambient neighborhood $N$ of the outer boundary. For the supplied collar $c:K\times[0,\eta)\to F$, the open set $c^{-1}(N)$ contains $K\times\{0\}$. A finite cover of the compact circle by product neighborhoods gives one $0<\delta<\eta$ with $c(K\times[0,\delta])\subset N$. Thus $\Psi$ fixes this sufficiently small restriction of the supplied collar; no fixedness of its entire image is asserted.

**Use only the concentric round shell.** The explicit map $(z,t)\mapsto(\varepsilon+(1-\varepsilon)t)z$ is a diffeomorphism $S^3\times[0,1]\to B^4\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon$. The inner boundary curve is the great circle $P\cap S^3_\varepsilon$, hence a standard unknot after radial rescaling; an orthonormal basis of $P$ extends by finite linear algebra to an oriented orthonormal basis of $\mathbb R^4$, giving an orientation-preserving linear rotation identifying it with the usual equator. Near the inner sphere the surface is a radial product in $P$, so this radial shell coordinate already supplies its product collar.

**Respect a restriction of the given outer surface collar.** For completeness the original outer surface collar need not be radial. In its smooth proper half-space chart the radial coordinate has nonzero inward derivative along a transverse collar direction. In a supplied parametrization of that collar, [F3] and compactness of its boundary circle therefore reparametrize it, for $r$ near $1$, as $(r f_r(\theta))$ with $f_r:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ a smooth embedding family and $f_1$ the original parametrized $K$. By [F1] on $S^3$, choose a smooth ambient family $G_r$ with $G_1=\mathrm{id}$ and $G_r f_1=f_r$. Choose a smooth function $h(r)$ equal to $r$ near $1$ and to $1$ near the inner edge of this thin outer collar, with values in the parameter interval where $G$ is defined. 3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.

Let $X$ be a four-dimensional manifold with boundary and let $W$ be a compact surface with boundary. An embedding $e:(W,\partial W)\to(X,\partial X)$ is proper when $e^{-1}(\partial X)=\partial W$. It is locally flat at an interior point of $W$ when there are neighborhoods of the point and its image and a homeomorphism of pairs from those neighborhoods to $(\mathbb R^4,\mathbb R^2)$, with the standard linear plane $\mathbb R^2\subset\mathbb R^4$. It is locally flat at a boundary point when there are such neighborhoods and a homeomorphism of pairs to $(\mathbb R^4_+,\mathbb R^2_+)$, where $\mathbb R^4_+=\{x_4\geq0\}$ and $\mathbb R^2_+=\{x_2=x_3=0,\ x_4\geq0\}$; the line $\partial\mathbb R^2_+$ lies in $\partial\mathbb R^4_+$. A collar of a boundary circle of $W$ is an embedding of that circle times $[0,\varepsilon)$ into $W$ that is the identity on the circle at parameter $0$; a concordance collar is required to agree with the corresponding product collar of the ambient end. A smooth proper surface has the analogous smooth charts and collars, which are also topological locally flat charts.

In ZF, let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be smooth, and let $a\in U$. If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open neighbourhoods $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that $f|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Writing $g=(f|_V)^{-1}$,
$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$
No choice axiom is used.

Its spatial vector field extends and integrates as in [F2], with time $t$ merely a smooth parameter. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface, with product collars and boundary the finite oriented links $-L_0$ and $L_1$ in the two ends. Components of $S$ and either boundary link may be empty. After an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller prescribed end collars, $S$ has a finite movie consisting of planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves R1, R2 and R3, births, oriented saddle band moves, and deaths. All exceptional times are distinct. The movie's actual smoothly embedded trace is ambient isotopic to the given $S$ relative to those collars, with its boundary orientations and parametrizations retained. Prescribed regular endpoint diagrams may be retained. This is movie existence; it asserts no equivalence theorem for two movies.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:C\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be a smooth
isotopy of a finite disjoint union of circles, constant near both ends, and
suppose both end projections under the fixed $\pi$ are regular. Arbitrarily
close to $F$ in the strong smooth topology there is such an isotopy $F'$, equal
to $F$ near the ends, whose projected slices have only these exceptional events:

(i) finitely many ordinary cusps, at distinct times; in a source coordinate
$x$, writing $g(x,t)=\pi F'(x,t)$, each satisfies
$g_x=0$, $\det(g_{xx},g_{xt})\ne0$ and
$\det(g_{xx},g_{xxx})\ne0$;

(ii) the **off-diagonal unordered** double-point locus is a smooth
one-dimensional manifold with boundary in the local-extension sense of
[[def-smooth-chart-atlas-and-structure-on-a-manifold-with-boundary]]; its boundary
consists exactly of the double points at $t=0,1$. Its interior is a manifold
without boundary, and its time projection has only finitely many
nondegenerate critical points, each an ordinary quadratic tangency of two
immersed branches;

(iii) finitely many transverse triple events, with all three pairs of
projected tangents independent, and no quadruple points.

No two exceptional events have the same time. All other slices are regular,
and between exceptional times their decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy.

Let $F'$ satisfy the general-position conditions of
[[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-links-can-be-put-in-general-position]], with
exceptional times $t_1<\cdots<t_N$. Immediately before and after each event,
its regular diagrams differ, up to planar isotopy, by one oriented
Reidemeister move: R1 at an ordinary cusp, R2 at a quadratic double tangency,
and R3 at a transverse triple event. The regular intervals contribute planar
isotopies, and the moves preserve the over/under and orientation data of $F'$.
Consequently the end diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of these moves.

derivations.claim: **A monotone target for the marked arc.** Choose a spatial stereographic chart containing the compact spatial image of $\gamma$: a smooth arc has null image in the three-sphere by the same Sard dimension argument used in [F3]. Write $\gamma(u)=(b(u),h(u))$ there and choose its collar parametrization so $h(u)=u$ near zero and one. The arc $\gamma_*(u)=(b(u),u)$ is embedded because its time coordinate is $u$. The interpolation $G(s,u)=(b(u),(1-s)h(u)+su)$ is a smooth homotopy fixed near the two endpoint collars. Away from those collars its time coordinate stays in $(0,1)$. It need not initially be an isotopy, so an additional general-position argument is necessary.

The result is an actual embedding isotopy from $\gamma$ to $\gamma_*$. Extend it by [F2], choosing the extended velocity zero near smaller end collars, and apply it to the whole $S$. It makes the marked arc monotone while retaining the collared marked boundary.

**A product strip about the track.** On the new surface, height has derivative one along $\gamma_*$. The implicit-function theorem supplies a neighborhood with coordinates $(t,v)$ in which height is exactly $t$ and the marked arc is $v=0$. Compactness gives one uniformly narrow strip; in the end collars it agrees with the specified product strip. In each spatial level its strip is an embedded interval through $b(t)$. Its nonzero spatial tangent at $v=0$ has a smooth unit direction $a(t)$. Complete that direction to a smooth spatial frame along the interval: start with one frame and transport an orthogonal frame by the smooth projection-commutator ODE, or solve the equivalent finite-dimensional orthogonal transport ODE. The interval has no monodromy obstruction. In its fiberwise tubular coordinates the strip differs from $v\mapsto b(t)+v a(t)$ by $O(v^2)$ with its first derivative $O(v)$, uniformly in $t$. Interpolating this error to zero inside a smaller strip, with a spatial cutoff in a slightly larger moving ball, is an embedding isotopy for a sufficiently small uniform width. Its spatial vector field extends and integrates as in [F2], with time $t$ merely a smooth parameter. Hence a level-preserving spatial coordinate family sends the marked track and a surrounding surface strip to a fixed straight model in one small three-ball. Choose the endpoint coordinate identifications to be its endpoint values; compatible prescribed long presentations need no change there. These are coordinate identifications, not an assertion that distinct physical endpoint marks were already the same point.

**Puncture at the mark and retain the collars.** Choose the fixed model so its central point is the stereographic point at infinity and its surface interval is a round circle through that point. Stereographic projection makes the punctured interval two fixed straight exterior rays. Remove a smaller open marked strip. The rest of the surface is a compact collared tangle cobordism in a fixed ball of $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$, with two fixed endpoint collars on the spatial ball boundary at every time. All other parts of the surface are disjoint from the retained strip; compactness after taking a slightly smaller strip provides a uniform separation. Extend the two spatial end rays by one fixed planar exterior closing arc outside a sufficiently large projection disk, marking a point on that arc. This closure represents exactly the deleted standard marked interval in its three-ball, with the same endpoint parametrizations. The compact part projects inside the large disk and the closing arc misses its interior. Consequently all later compactly supported projection events can occur inside that disk while the mark and a neighborhood of it remain fixed outside.

**Finite Morse events relative to the strip.** Run the height part of the construction in [F3] on the compact tangle part. All bumps have support outside the fixed tangle-end collars and the removed marked strip. Where those collars are protected, height is the product coordinate and has no critical point. On the remaining finite chart cores the bump-linear perturbations of height span each cotangent fiber exactly as in [F3]; [F1] therefore gives a Morse height. The critical points are finite, their values can be separated by disjoint supported bumps, and sufficiently small perturbations remain embeddings with an actual ambient trace isotopy. Their tangent-plane projections and complementary regular branches can be made generic by spatial bumps on the same compact part. The resulting birth, saddle and death disks lie inside the large projection disk. The long end collars and the marked closing arc are fixed. These are the actual local models of [F3], with a protected regular boundary added, not any assumption that a mark survives an arbitrary unbased movie.

**Finite projection events and the actual trace.** On each complementary regular-height slab choose the normalized gradient equal to the fixed product field near the long ends; patching the product field with the normalized field preserves $dh(X)=1$. Its flow gives an isotopy of compact tangles fixed near their ends. Flatten small strips at the cut times by the interpolation $(F_{(1-s)t+s\rho(t)}(x),t)$ from [F3]; its time coordinate is still $t$, so it is an embedding isotopy. Apply the finite-jet proof in [F4] relatively to the fixed exterior arc and end collars. The needed parameter bumps prescribe independent jets at the moving source points. No forbidden event can involve a point on the exterior arc and a compact point, because their projections are separated by the large disk; the fixed joining collars are straight, with a protected regular neighborhood. Events wholly in the compact part have exactly the evaluation submersions and deleted-diagonal bounds of [F4]. Hence there are finitely many ordinary R1/R2/R3 events, fixed near slab ends; identify them by the second supplier in [F4]. Small spatial interpolation retains the actual traced surface, and [F2] extends it relative to every protected collar. Thus all the resulting Reidemeister support disks also miss the marked arc.

Glue the finitely many critical intervals and regular slabs along their stationary cuts. Choose their exceptional times distinct as in [F3]. The fixed exterior closing arc supplies the mark in every frame, including any frame with additional circles, and none of its points participates in a birth, saddle or death. Undo the spatial coordinate family of step 3.1 and the marked-strip replacement to compare the trace: all actual perturbations were ambient isotopies relative to the retained collars, and the coordinate family has the explicitly recorded endpoint identifications. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented collared embedded annulus from a knot $K_0$ to a knot $K_1$. Let $\gamma\subset S$ be a smooth properly embedded arc joining their specified marked points and equal to their vertical marked intervals in smaller end collars. There exist based regular diagrams representing these endpoint knots and a finite oriented movie between them, consisting of planar isotopies, R1, R2, R3, births, saddles and deaths, with a marked point in every frame. The marked track is strictly increasing in height, never dies, never lies at a diagram crossing, and misses the closed support disks of every exceptional move. Every regular interval also keeps a neighborhood of the mark fixed in its chosen diagram coordinates.

More precisely, first an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller end collars carries the given marked surface to one with monotone marked arc. A smooth level-preserving change of spatial coordinates then puts a neighborhood of that arc into a fixed exterior closing-arc position. The movie trace, transported back by those same coordinates, is ambient isotopic to the original marked $S$ relative to the smaller end collars. Its endpoint diagrams and their marked parametrizations use the corresponding endpoint coordinate identifications. One may retain prescribed endpoint diagrams already in this compatible long-tangle presentation. The conclusion does not assert a based Reidemeister sequence between arbitrary prescribed planar endpoint diagrams or between arbitrary basepoint presentations, and asserts no movie-independence theorem for algebraic maps.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:C\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be a smooth
isotopy of a finite disjoint union of circles, constant near both ends, and
suppose both end projections under the fixed $\pi$ are regular. Arbitrarily
close to $F$ in the strong smooth topology there is such an isotopy $F'$, equal
to $F$ near the ends, whose projected slices have only these exceptional events:

(i) finitely many ordinary cusps, at distinct times; in a source coordinate
$x$, writing $g(x,t)=\pi F'(x,t)$, each satisfies
$g_x=0$, $\det(g_{xx},g_{xt})\ne0$ and
$\det(g_{xx},g_{xxx})\ne0$;

(ii) the **off-diagonal unordered** double-point locus is a smooth
one-dimensional manifold with boundary in the local-extension sense of
[[def-smooth-chart-atlas-and-structure-on-a-manifold-with-boundary]]; its boundary
consists exactly of the double points at $t=0,1$. Its interior is a manifold
without boundary, and its time projection has only finitely many
nondegenerate critical points, each an ordinary quadratic tangency of two
immersed branches;

(iii) finitely many transverse triple events, with all three pairs of
projected tangents independent, and no quadruple points.

No two exceptional events have the same time. All other slices are regular,
and between exceptional times their decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy.

Let $F'$ satisfy the general-position conditions of
[[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-links-can-be-put-in-general-position]], with
exceptional times $t_1<\cdots<t_N$. Immediately before and after each event,
its regular diagrams differ, up to planar isotopy, by one oriented
Reidemeister move: R1 at an ordinary cusp, R2 at a quadratic double tangency,
and R3 at a transverse triple event. The regular intervals contribute planar
isotopies, and the moves preserve the over/under and orientation data of $F'$.
Consequently the end diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of these moves.

derivations.claim: **Small marked arcs and their relative center–tangent data.** Parametrize a uniformly small marked interval by oriented arclength $v$ near zero, smoothly in the isotopy parameter $t$; the resulting reparametrization changes neither knot nor mark and is stationary in the end collars. Let $b(t)=F(0,t)$ and let $u(t)$ be its unit tangent. Identify $S^3$ with unit quaternions. The imaginary unit quaternion $c(t)=b(t)^{-1}u(t)$ lies in $S^2$, and $(b(t),c(t))$ is a smooth loop in $S^3\times S^2$, constant in the end collars. The two endpoint marked arcs are the same by hypothesis. In exponential coordinates at $b(t)$ the small actual arc has the form $vu(t)+O(v^2)$, with derivative $u(t)+O(v)$ uniformly in $t$. Interpolating its error to zero gives a smooth family of embedded intervals for a sufficiently small uniform width: projection onto $u(t)$ has strictly positive derivative. This interpolation is stationary in the end collars if their common model is taken to be the geodesic round arc, as stipulated. Its inverse will later restore the actual marked germ.

**An explicit contraction fixes both parameter ends.** A smooth loop in either $S^d$, $d=2,3$, misses a point. Indeed a derivative bound makes its $n$ equal parameter intervals map into $n$ balls of radius $C/n$; their total spherical $d$-volume is at most $C'n^{1-d}$, which tends to zero. They cannot cover the positive-volume sphere. Choose one omitted point for each of the two loops from step 1.1. Stereographic coordinates from those points send each loop into Euclidean space. The straight interpolation from its constant endpoint value to its value at $t$ contracts it through loops constant on the same end collars; inverse stereographic projection gives smooth loops $b_s(t),c_s(t)$, with $s=0$ constant and $s=1$ the given data. Thus $$A_{s,t}(v)=b_s(t)\bigl(\cos v+c_s(t)\sin v\bigr)$$ is a smooth family of geodesic marked interval embeddings, with $A_{0,t}$ the common standard arc and $A_{s,t}$ equal to it in both end collars. Concatenate with the inverse error interpolation in step 1.1, using stationary smooth parameter joins. This constructs a two-parameter family of embedded intervals from the constant common arc to the actual moving marked arcs; at $t$ in either end collar the entire family is the constant arc.

**Relative ambient coordinates really are identity at both ends.** Extend the velocity in the contraction parameter $s$ of step 2.1 by the actual construction in [F1], with $t$ an additional parameter. To spell out the relative point: the track in $S^3\times[0,1]_s\times[0,1]_t$ is embedded because its last two coordinates retain $s,t$ and each interval slice is embedded. In finite track charts extend the three spatial velocity components constantly in normal coordinates, patch by a smooth partition, and apply a compact cutoff equal to one on the smaller interval track. The prescribed velocity is zero on both $t$ end collars; choose all extended components zero there, using charts of the constant product arc on those collars and a cutoff in $t$ on their complement. Integrate in $s$. Uniqueness of the ODE gives a smooth family $H_t$ of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms with $H_t(A_{0,t})$ the actual marked interval and $H_t=\mathrm{id}$ on both time end collars. Consequently $H_t^{-1}F_t$ is a knot isotopy retaining exactly the given endpoints and fixing one common marked interval for every $t$. This contraction argument is necessary: simply extending the moving interval in the parameter $t$ would not by itself force the terminal ambient map to be the identity.

**Puncture without changing height or endpoints.** Apply the product-strip and puncture construction of [F2] to this fixed common interval, with spatial coordinates independent of $t$. In a smaller neighborhood the knots agree with that interval for all $t$; compactness gives uniform separation from the rest after shortening it once. Puncturing at its central point gives an isotopy of compact long tangles, fixed on their two spatial end collars, closed by one fixed exterior arc carrying the mark. The spatial coordinate changes in step 3.1 were level-preserving, so its trace is still exactly a cylinder of knot embeddings with time coordinate $t$. In particular the restriction of time to this cylinder has nonzero derivative everywhere. There is no need for a Morse perturbation, and none is made. There is an explicit planar endpoint comparison if the displayed closed diagrams initially use a pole in the adjacent face rather than the spatial puncture at the mark. Write their common round compact projection disk as $D=\{|z|\le R\}$ and their common marked point as $p$, where $|p|>R$. Choose a small marked germ and $\delta>0$ so that its closed neighborhood misses $W=\{|z|<R+\delta\}$. Set $$b_u=\frac{uR^2}{\overline p},\qquad f_u(z)=\frac{z-b_u}{1-\overline b_u z/R^2},\qquad 0\le u\le1.$$ These are disk automorphisms, starting at the identity: on $|z|=R$ one has $|z-b_u|^2=R^2|1-\overline b_u z/R^2|^2$, and their inverse fractional linear maps have the same disk property. Their complex derivative has nonzero numerator $1-|b_u|^2/R^2>0$. Their pole is $p/u$, with infinity at $u=0$, so it stays outside $D$ and ends at the marked point. Thus $f_u|_D$ is an actual smooth isotopy of compact disk embeddings onto $D$, including $u=1$. It is an orientation-preserving coordinate chart on the punctured projection sphere. Its endpoint pole is the spatial puncture point; postcomposition by a positive planar similarity identifies it with a rotation-induced stereographic chart with that pole if such a chart is used for the spatial coordinates. One may instead retain this very chart in the puncture construction. Apply [F1] to $f_u|_D$ in the plane, with extension support in $W$. Its disk velocity is tangent to the boundary; the extension theorem for a compact source with boundary applies and gives an ambient plane isotopy $\Phi_u$ equal to $f_u$ on $D$ and identity outside $W$. Consequently it fixes the specified marked germ pointwise throughout. Choose the long closing arc to be $\Phi_1$ of the original common exterior arc. It is outside $D$, since $\Phi_1$ preserves $D$, and retains exactly the same marked germ. This supplies protected planar isotopies from the displayed endpoints to the punctured-and-reclosed endpoints; prepend and append those isotopies. For two normalized endpoints use the same $D,p,b_u,\Phi_u$ and closing arc. No arbitrary ambient extension or equality of different planar charts is being assumed: both the prescribed endpoint diagrams and their fixed marked germ are retained by the recorded relative extension.

**Relative finite projection genericity.** Repeat the family of [F3] on this compact tangle isotopy with bumps zero on smaller parameter end collars and spatial tangle-end collars. At every movable source point these bumps are positive, so the same finite monomial Hermite interpolation prescribes the required independent jets; its evaluations at protected source points are not needed. The exterior closing arc and the two joining collars have fixed regular projection, separated from the compact moving portion. Thus no bad projection stratum involving the protected mark is present. On the moving portion the cusp, tangent-double and triple equations, exclusions of their coincidences and higher degeneracies, and deleted-diagonal estimates are precisely those proved in [F3]. Arbitrarily small parameter choices give finitely many separated generic events relative the stationary endpoint diagrams. The perturbations change spatial coordinates of the slice embeddings only, so their trace remains a height-submersive cylinder. Straight interpolation between the original and sufficiently close perturbed slice maps is an embedding isotopy by the uniform local immersion and distant-pair separation bounds used in [F3]. It is fixed on every protected collar.

The event identification in [F3] gives only oriented R1, R2 and R3 moves; between them the projected decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy. Each exceptional event has compact support inside the projection disk and therefore misses the fixed marked exterior arc. The finite time list yields the required sequence. No surface critical point has been introduced, so births, saddles and deaths do not occur. Undoing $H_t^{-1}$ identifies its trace with the given marked isotopy, up to the small relative perturbation in step 5.1. Since $H_t$ is identity on both end collars, the spatial endpoint identifications are retained exactly; the explicitly recorded planar endpoint isotopies in step 4.1 return the displayed prescribed diagrams. This proves the stated relative comparison and no algebraic map assertion.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented collared embedded annulus from a knot $K_0$ to a knot $K_1$. Let $\gamma\subset S$ be a smooth properly embedded arc joining their specified marked points and equal to their vertical marked intervals in smaller end collars. There exist based regular diagrams representing these endpoint knots and a finite oriented movie between them, consisting of planar isotopies, R1, R2, R3, births, saddles and deaths, with a marked point in every frame. The marked track is strictly increasing in height, never dies, never lies at a diagram crossing, and misses the closed support disks of every exceptional move. Every regular interval also keeps a neighborhood of the mark fixed in its chosen diagram coordinates.

More precisely, first an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller end collars carries the given marked surface to one with monotone marked arc. A smooth level-preserving change of spatial coordinates then puts a neighborhood of that arc into a fixed exterior closing-arc position. The movie trace, transported back by those same coordinates, is ambient isotopic to the original marked $S$ relative to the smaller end collars. Its endpoint diagrams and their marked parametrizations use the corresponding endpoint coordinate identifications. One may retain prescribed endpoint diagrams already in this compatible long-tangle presentation. The conclusion does not assert a based Reidemeister sequence between arbitrary prescribed planar endpoint diagrams or between arbitrary basepoint presentations, and asserts no movie-independence theorem for algebraic maps.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $F:C\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be a smooth
isotopy of a finite disjoint union of circles, constant near both ends, and
suppose both end projections under the fixed $\pi$ are regular. Arbitrarily
close to $F$ in the strong smooth topology there is such an isotopy $F'$, equal
to $F$ near the ends, whose projected slices have only these exceptional events:

(i) finitely many ordinary cusps, at distinct times; in a source coordinate
$x$, writing $g(x,t)=\pi F'(x,t)$, each satisfies
$g_x=0$, $\det(g_{xx},g_{xt})\ne0$ and
$\det(g_{xx},g_{xxx})\ne0$;

(ii) the **off-diagonal unordered** double-point locus is a smooth
one-dimensional manifold with boundary in the local-extension sense of
[[def-smooth-chart-atlas-and-structure-on-a-manifold-with-boundary]]; its boundary
consists exactly of the double points at $t=0,1$. Its interior is a manifold
without boundary, and its time projection has only finitely many
nondegenerate critical points, each an ordinary quadratic tangency of two
immersed branches;

(iii) finitely many transverse triple events, with all three pairs of
projected tangents independent, and no quadruple points.

No two exceptional events have the same time. All other slices are regular,
and between exceptional times their decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy.

Let $F'$ satisfy the general-position conditions of
[[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-links-can-be-put-in-general-position]], with
exceptional times $t_1<\cdots<t_N$. Immediately before and after each event,
its regular diagrams differ, up to planar isotopy, by one oriented
Reidemeister move: R1 at an ordinary cusp, R2 at a quadratic double tangency,
and R3 at a transverse triple event. The regular intervals contribute planar
isotopies, and the moves preserve the over/under and orientation data of $F'$.
Consequently the end diagrams are connected by a finite sequence of these moves.

derivations.claim: **Small marked arcs and their relative center–tangent data.** Parametrize a uniformly small marked interval by oriented arclength $v$ near zero, smoothly in the isotopy parameter $t$; the resulting reparametrization changes neither knot nor mark and is stationary in the end collars. Let $b(t)=F(0,t)$ and let $u(t)$ be its unit tangent. Identify $S^3$ with unit quaternions. The imaginary unit quaternion $c(t)=b(t)^{-1}u(t)$ lies in $S^2$, and $(b(t),c(t))$ is a smooth loop in $S^3\times S^2$, constant in the end collars. The two endpoint marked arcs are the same by hypothesis. In exponential coordinates at $b(t)$ the small actual arc has the form $vu(t)+O(v^2)$, with derivative $u(t)+O(v)$ uniformly in $t$. Interpolating its error to zero gives a smooth family of embedded intervals for a sufficiently small uniform width: projection onto $u(t)$ has strictly positive derivative. This interpolation is stationary in the end collars if their common model is taken to be the geodesic round arc, as stipulated. Its inverse will later restore the actual marked germ.

**An explicit contraction fixes both parameter ends.** A smooth loop in either $S^d$, $d=2,3$, misses a point. Indeed a derivative bound makes its $n$ equal parameter intervals map into $n$ balls of radius $C/n$; their total spherical $d$-volume is at most $C'n^{1-d}$, which tends to zero. They cannot cover the positive-volume sphere. Choose one omitted point for each of the two loops from step 1.1. Stereographic coordinates from those points send each loop into Euclidean space. The straight interpolation from its constant endpoint value to its value at $t$ contracts it through loops constant on the same end collars; inverse stereographic projection gives smooth loops $b_s(t),c_s(t)$, with $s=0$ constant and $s=1$ the given data. Thus $$A_{s,t}(v)=b_s(t)\bigl(\cos v+c_s(t)\sin v\bigr)$$ is a smooth family of geodesic marked interval embeddings, with $A_{0,t}$ the common standard arc and $A_{s,t}$ equal to it in both end collars. Concatenate with the inverse error interpolation in step 1.1, using stationary smooth parameter joins. This constructs a two-parameter family of embedded intervals from the constant common arc to the actual moving marked arcs; at $t$ in either end collar the entire family is the constant arc.

**Relative ambient coordinates really are identity at both ends.** Extend the velocity in the contraction parameter $s$ of step 2.1 by the actual construction in [F1], with $t$ an additional parameter. To spell out the relative point: the track in $S^3\times[0,1]_s\times[0,1]_t$ is embedded because its last two coordinates retain $s,t$ and each interval slice is embedded. In finite track charts extend the three spatial velocity components constantly in normal coordinates, patch by a smooth partition, and apply a compact cutoff equal to one on the smaller interval track. The prescribed velocity is zero on both $t$ end collars; choose all extended components zero there, using charts of the constant product arc on those collars and a cutoff in $t$ on their complement. Integrate in $s$. Uniqueness of the ODE gives a smooth family $H_t$ of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms with $H_t(A_{0,t})$ the actual marked interval and $H_t=\mathrm{id}$ on both time end collars. Consequently $H_t^{-1}F_t$ is a knot isotopy retaining exactly the given endpoints and fixing one common marked interval for every $t$. This contraction argument is necessary: simply extending the moving interval in the parameter $t$ would not by itself force the terminal ambient map to be the identity.

**Puncture without changing height or endpoints.** Apply the product-strip and puncture construction of [F2] to this fixed common interval, with spatial coordinates independent of $t$. In a smaller neighborhood the knots agree with that interval for all $t$; compactness gives uniform separation from the rest after shortening it once. Puncturing at its central point gives an isotopy of compact long tangles, fixed on their two spatial end collars, closed by one fixed exterior arc carrying the mark. The spatial coordinate changes in step 3.1 were level-preserving, so its trace is still exactly a cylinder of knot embeddings with time coordinate $t$. In particular the restriction of time to this cylinder has nonzero derivative everywhere. There is no need for a Morse perturbation, and none is made. There is an explicit planar endpoint comparison if the displayed closed diagrams initially use a pole in the adjacent face rather than the spatial puncture at the mark. Write their common round compact projection disk as $D=\{|z|\le R\}$ and their common marked point as $p$, where $|p|>R$. Choose a small marked germ and $\delta>0$ so that its closed neighborhood misses $W=\{|z|<R+\delta\}$. Set $$b_u=\frac{uR^2}{\overline p},\qquad f_u(z)=\frac{z-b_u}{1-\overline b_u z/R^2},\qquad 0\le u\le1.$$ These are disk automorphisms, starting at the identity: on $|z|=R$ one has $|z-b_u|^2=R^2|1-\overline b_u z/R^2|^2$, and their inverse fractional linear maps have the same disk property. Their complex derivative has nonzero numerator $1-|b_u|^2/R^2>0$. Their pole is $p/u$, with infinity at $u=0$, so it stays outside $D$ and ends at the marked point. Thus $f_u|_D$ is an actual smooth isotopy of compact disk embeddings onto $D$, including $u=1$. It is an orientation-preserving coordinate chart on the punctured projection sphere. Its endpoint pole is the spatial puncture point; postcomposition by a positive planar similarity identifies it with a rotation-induced stereographic chart with that pole if such a chart is used for the spatial coordinates. One may instead retain this very chart in the puncture construction. Apply [F1] to $f_u|_D$ in the plane, with extension support in $W$. Its disk velocity is tangent to the boundary; the extension theorem for a compact source with boundary applies and gives an ambient plane isotopy $\Phi_u$ equal to $f_u$ on $D$ and identity outside $W$. Consequently it fixes the specified marked germ pointwise throughout. Choose the long closing arc to be $\Phi_1$ of the original common exterior arc. It is outside $D$, since $\Phi_1$ preserves $D$, and retains exactly the same marked germ. This supplies protected planar isotopies from the displayed endpoints to the punctured-and-reclosed endpoints; prepend and append those isotopies. For two normalized endpoints use the same $D,p,b_u,\Phi_u$ and closing arc. No arbitrary ambient extension or equality of different planar charts is being assumed: both the prescribed endpoint diagrams and their fixed marked germ are retained by the recorded relative extension.

**Relative finite projection genericity.** Repeat the family of [F3] on this compact tangle isotopy with bumps zero on smaller parameter end collars and spatial tangle-end collars. At every movable source point these bumps are positive, so the same finite monomial Hermite interpolation prescribes the required independent jets; its evaluations at protected source points are not needed. The exterior closing arc and the two joining collars have fixed regular projection, separated from the compact moving portion. Thus no bad projection stratum involving the protected mark is present. On the moving portion the cusp, tangent-double and triple equations, exclusions of their coincidences and higher degeneracies, and deleted-diagonal estimates are precisely those proved in [F3]. Arbitrarily small parameter choices give finitely many separated generic events relative the stationary endpoint diagrams. The perturbations change spatial coordinates of the slice embeddings only, so their trace remains a height-submersive cylinder. Straight interpolation between the original and sufficiently close perturbed slice maps is an embedding isotopy by the uniform local immersion and distant-pair separation bounds used in [F3]. It is fixed on every protected collar.

The event identification in [F3] gives only oriented R1, R2 and R3 moves; between them the projected decorated diagrams vary by planar isotopy. Each exceptional event has compact support inside the projection disk and therefore misses the fixed marked exterior arc. The finite time list yields the required sequence. No surface critical point has been introduced, so births, saddles and deaths do not occur. Undoing $H_t^{-1}$ identifies its trace with the given marked isotopy, up to the small relative perturbation in step 5.1. Since $H_t$ is identity on both end collars, the spatial endpoint identifications are retained exactly; the explicitly recorded planar endpoint isotopies in step 4.1 return the displayed prescribed diagrams. This proves the stated relative comparison and no algebraic map assertion.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

**Input:** a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ and a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on its crossing set. A diagram object is supplied as mathematical input; this procedure does not parse a serialized string.

**Output:** the normalized bigraded Khovanov cochain module $C^{i,j}(D)$ and its candidate differential $d:C^{i,j}(D)\to C^{i+1,j}(D)$, constructed by the following finite instructions.

1. Enumerate every state $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$ once. Form the crossingless resolution by using the A-smoothing at $v(c)=0$ and the B-smoothing at $v(c)=1$.
2. For each state, create one tensor factor of the integral Frobenius algebra for each resolution circle and place the resulting tensor product in cohomological degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum degree $|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$ for its circle labels $a$.
3. For each state and each crossing $c_j$ with $v(c_j)=0$, create the edge to $v+e_j$. Apply multiplication if that smoothing change merges two circles, comultiplication if it splits one circle, the identity on other tensor factors, and the sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. Sum the edge maps out of every state to obtain $d$.
4. Return the finite direct sum of the state modules with these degrees and maps. The square-zero property is the separate local lemma named by `justified_by`.

$$
$$

oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the

orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$

the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$

oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never

Since $\sigma(w+e_j)/\sigma(w)=(-1)^{j-1}$, this makes every edge commute with the transposed original edge. It is therefore an actual cochain isomorphism, including cube signs. Conversely a homology functional vanishing on classes represented by cycles in $F^{1-p}C$ defines a functional on the sum of the cycle space and $F^{1-p}C$, using its given values on cycles and zero on the latter subspace. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented knot diagram with ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ and a marked point $p$ away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

The square condition is that the sum of the two signed saddle composites around each two-dimensional cube face is zero. An edge sign function satisfying it is called square-compatible; existence and invariance require separate proofs.

Let $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, with $\deg_q(h)=\deg_q(X)=-2$. Its Frobenius structure has unit $\eta(1)=1$, counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, quotient-ring multiplication, and comultiplication
$$ \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h\,1\otimes1,\qquad \Delta(X)=X\otimes X. $$
Applying these operations to the same normalized cube gives the Bar–Natan cochain complex $C_h(D)$, with circle labels $1,X$ of quantum degrees $1,-1$ and the same normalized state shifts; it is a complex of free $\mathbb R$-modules, and the marked circle acts by multiplication by $X$.

Put $\mathbb B=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)=\mathbb R/(2,h)$. Modulo $2$, the odd exterior basis vector $C_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge C_{i_r}$ corresponds to the even tensor state labeling the selected circles $C_{i_j}$ by $X$ and all other circles by $1$. This statewise bijection defines the candidate comparison $f_D:C_o(D)\otimes\mathbb F_2\to C_h(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B$ after setting $h=0$.

A **local even–odd (LEO) triple** is a triple $(C,D,f)$ consisting of a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $C$ free over $\mathbb A$, a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $D$ free over $\mathbb R$, and a bigraded $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy equivalence
$$ f:C\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_2\longrightarrow D\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B, \qquad \mathbb B=\mathbb R/(2,h)=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2), $$
such that $D[h^{-1}]$ is chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ to one free rank-one module supported in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree. For a based knot diagram the intended candidate is $(C_o(D),C_h(D),f_D)$, where $f_D$ identifies the reduced edge maps modulo $2$ and $h$; its satisfaction of the homotopy and localization conditions is a separate theorem.

A local map $(C,D,f)\to(C',D',f')$ is a pair of bigraded module chain maps $\alpha:C\to C'$ and $\beta:D\to D'$ such that $\beta[h^{-1}]$ is a chain homotopy equivalence and the square induced by $f,f',\alpha,\beta$ after quotienting by $(2,h)$ commutes up to an $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy. Two LEO triples are locally equivalent when there is a local map in each direction.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented knot diagram with ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ and a marked point $p$ away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

The square condition is that the sum of the two signed saddle composites around each two-dimensional cube face is zero. An edge sign function satisfying it is called square-compatible; existence and invariance require separate proofs.

Let $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, with $\deg_q(h)=\deg_q(X)=-2$. Its Frobenius structure has unit $\eta(1)=1$, counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, quotient-ring multiplication, and comultiplication
$$ \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h\,1\otimes1,\qquad \Delta(X)=X\otimes X. $$
Applying these operations to the same normalized cube gives the Bar–Natan cochain complex $C_h(D)$, with circle labels $1,X$ of quantum degrees $1,-1$ and the same normalized state shifts; it is a complex of free $\mathbb R$-modules, and the marked circle acts by multiplication by $X$.

Put $\mathbb B=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)=\mathbb R/(2,h)$. Modulo $2$, the odd exterior basis vector $C_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge C_{i_r}$ corresponds to the even tensor state labeling the selected circles $C_{i_j}$ by $X$ and all other circles by $1$. This statewise bijection defines the candidate comparison $f_D:C_o(D)\otimes\mathbb F_2\to C_h(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B$ after setting $h=0$.

$$ f:C\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_2\longrightarrow D\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B, \qquad \mathbb B=\mathbb R/(2,h)=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2), $$

For a based knot diagram the intended candidate is $(C_o(D),C_h(D),f_D)$, where $f_D$ identifies the reduced edge maps modulo $2$ and $h$; its satisfaction of the homotopy and localization conditions is a separate theorem.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every finite regular based oriented knot diagram, the odd exterior-algebra cube admits a square-compatible edge assignment and defines a bigraded cochain complex; its mod-2 reduction is chain homotopy equivalent as a marked $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-complex to the Bar–Natan complex reduced modulo $(2,h)$. After inverting $h$, the Bar–Natan complex is chain homotopy equivalent to one free rank-one module in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree over the localized coefficient algebra. Based diagram changes preserve the odd complex up to chain homotopy equivalence, and pointed connected sums give the chain-level tensor product over $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ for the odd complex and over $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$ for the Bar–Natan complex, in each case with the quantum shift $\{-1\}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The set of smooth oriented knot concordance classes in the standard three-sphere is an abelian group under connected sum, with identity the standard unknot and inverse of $[K]$ represented by the reverse mirror $K^\dagger$. Separately, the set of locally flat topological oriented knot concordance classes is an abelian group under connected sum, with the same identity and inverse convention.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let a finite oriented based regular link diagram, with its ordered crossing disks and crossing arrows, lie on an oriented two-sphere. Choose any two orientation-preserving planar coordinate presentations whose omitted points miss the diagram and all crossing disks. Transport the diagram, crossing arrows, over/under information and mark by these coordinates; keep the same crossing order. Circle relabelling gives grading-preserving marked-module chain isomorphisms between their integral odd complexes with transported full admissible edge signs, and between their integral Bar–Natan complexes. In particular the full odd face prescription, including zero-composite faces, is unchanged by the choice of omitted point.

For independently chosen edge assignments satisfying that full prescription, compose the odd relabelling with vertexwise signs. The resulting odd and Bar–Natan isomorphisms have inverse maps, are respectively right linear over $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, and give a strictly commuting square under the statewise reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$. Their inverses give the inverse square. Whenever the endpoint triples satisfy the LEO hypotheses, these maps therefore give local maps in both directions; this applies in particular to knot triples once their separate foundations have been established. The Bar–Natan maps are already chain isomorphisms before localization. The construction is finite and requires no choice axiom. This assertion concerns recharting the same spherical diagram, not transporting a mark through a crossing of a fixed planar diagram.

Assume countable choice. Every prescribed finite regular oriented knot diagram with a specified marked point away from its crossings admits a compatible long endpoint presentation by finitely many planar isotopies and one orientation-preserving spherical rotation recharting. All crossing labels, crossing arrows if specified, strand orientations, over/under data and the mark are transported. No crossing is created, removed, or passed through the mark. The final planar diagram has a round disk containing every crossing and all of the diagram except a single crossing-free exterior closing arc carrying the mark; the disk boundary meets the diagram transversely in exactly two points. A neighborhood of that arc can be used as the protected marked neighborhood in a long-tangle movie.

The recharting omits a point in a face adjacent to the marked germ. Its spherical rotation extends by an explicit orientation-preserving linear map of $S^3$, and the planar normalizations have actual spatial coordinate lifts. Thus the construction records an orientation-preserving spatial identification of the represented marked endpoint knot, rather than declaring its coordinate identifications to be identities. A representative can be chosen with the exterior arc at constant projection height and with product collars at its two cut points. This is a geometric existence assertion. It asserts neither a purely planar protected Reidemeister comparison nor an algebraic invariance theorem. The construction uses only finite selections and explicit maps, so in fact introduces no choice beyond the stated branch.

Assume countable choice. Let $F:S^1\times[0,1]\to S^3$ be a smooth isotopy of oriented knots, stationary in end collars, with a specified marked source point. Suppose its two endpoint diagrams are regular compatible long presentations with the same standard oriented exterior marked arc, parametrized identically on a neighborhood of that point. Use the corresponding spatial endpoint coordinates, in which this common marked arc is a standard small round arc through the stereographic point at infinity; its puncture is closed in the planar diagrams by the same standard exterior arc. Then these prescribed endpoint diagrams are related by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented R1, R2 and R3 moves, whose closed support disks miss the mark. The marked neighborhood remains fixed. There are no births, saddles or deaths. The movie represents the given marked isotopy up to a spatial coordinate family equal to the identity in both end collars and a small isotopy relative those collars.

Here compatible long endpoints include the displayed common oriented arc and its spatial coordinate identifications. This statement does not silently identify arbitrary physical endpoint coordinates. Spherical endpoint recharting may first be used to choose such common compatible presentations; no algebraic invariance of that recharting or of these movies is asserted here.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented collared embedded annulus from a knot $K_0$ to a knot $K_1$. Let $\gamma\subset S$ be a smooth properly embedded arc joining their specified marked points and equal to their vertical marked intervals in smaller end collars. There exist based regular diagrams representing these endpoint knots and a finite oriented movie between them, consisting of planar isotopies, R1, R2, R3, births, saddles and deaths, with a marked point in every frame. The marked track is strictly increasing in height, never dies, never lies at a diagram crossing, and misses the closed support disks of every exceptional move. Every regular interval also keeps a neighborhood of the mark fixed in its chosen diagram coordinates.

More precisely, first an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller end collars carries the given marked surface to one with monotone marked arc. A smooth level-preserving change of spatial coordinates then puts a neighborhood of that arc into a fixed exterior closing-arc position. The movie trace, transported back by those same coordinates, is ambient isotopic to the original marked $S$ relative to the smaller end collars. Its endpoint diagrams and their marked parametrizations use the corresponding endpoint coordinate identifications. One may retain prescribed endpoint diagrams already in this compatible long-tangle presentation. The conclusion does not assert a based Reidemeister sequence between arbitrary prescribed planar endpoint diagrams or between arbitrary basepoint presentations, and asserts no movie-independence theorem for algebraic maps.

Let a finite oriented link-cobordism movie carry a marked point continuously through its regular levels, with its trace disjoint from all elementary move disks, and with the marked component never dying. Use the odd cubes with the prescribed full face signs and the integral Bar–Natan cubes over $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$. This movie admits an integral odd map, linear for the marked right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action, and an integral marked $\mathbb R$-linear Bar–Natan map. They have cohomological degree zero and quantum degree the Euler characteristic of the movie, and their reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ agree under the statewise comparison. For a connected oriented concordance between knots the localized Bar–Natan map is a chain homotopy equivalence over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$. A localized knot complex retracts over that ring onto one free rank-one module in cohomological degree zero and odd quantum parity. All these statements concern the supplied movie; no independence from its presentation is asserted. The finite algebraic constructions use no choice axiom.

Let two finite based knot diagrams be joined along their marked arcs in a planar pointed connected-sum diagram, without new crossings. The odd complexes admit a normalized bigraded right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain isomorphism
$$ C_o(D_1)\otimes_{\mathbb A}C_o(D_2)\{-1\}\ \cong\ C_o(D_1\#D_2), $$
and the Bar–Natan complexes admit the corresponding marked $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$-linear chain isomorphism. In the odd case the induced signs realize the full prescribed face products, so admissible sign comparison applies, including zero-composite faces. The two isomorphisms agree after reduction modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ under the statewise comparison. Their construction is finite and choice-free.

derivations.claim: Local equivalence is reflexive because each triple has its identity local map, symmetric by its definition as maps in both directions, and transitive because the composites of local maps remain module chain maps, their localized Bar–Natan maps are composites of homotopy equivalences, and the two mod-$(2,h)$ squares compose up to the sum of their module-linear homotopies. Thus local equivalence is an equivalence relation.

The tensor product of two LEO triples is again a LEO triple: tensoring finite free complexes preserves finite freeness, tensoring the reductions gives the homotopy equivalence $f\otimes f'$, and tensoring the localized rank-one equivalences gives a rank-one equivalence over the localized coefficient algebra. Tensor products of local maps are local maps because tensor products preserve chain homotopies and homotopy equivalences between these free localized complexes. Hence the shifted tensor product is associative and respects local-equivalence classes. The graded symmetry $u\otimes v\mapsto(-1)^{|u||v|}v\otimes u$ gives commutativity, and the unknot triple is the unit because its complexes are $\mathbb A\{1\}$ and $\mathbb R\{1\}$.

For $T=(C,D,f)$ define $T^*=(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb A}(C,\mathbb A)\{2\},\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(D,\mathbb R)\{2\},f^*)$, where $f^*$ is the transpose induced by a homotopy inverse $g$ to the reduced equivalence $f$. Finite freeness lets dualization commute with reduction and localization; it preserves chain homotopies and chain homotopy equivalences. Thus $T^*$ satisfies the LEO conditions, and dualizing both maps and the module-linear homotopy in a local-map square gives a local map in the reverse direction. The finite-free tensor-Hom isomorphisms identify $T\otimes T^*$ with $(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb A}(C,C)\{1\},\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(D,D)\{1\},F)$, where on reductions $F(\eta)=f\eta g$. The coevaluation maps from the unknot triple send $1$ to $\mathrm{id}_C$ and $\mathrm{id}_D$. The reduced square commutes up to the module-linear homotopy $H$ from $fg\simeq\mathrm{id}_D$, since $F(\mathrm{id}_C)=fg$. After inverting $h$, the BN coevaluation map $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R[h^{-1}]}(D[h^{-1}],D[h^{-1}])$ sends $1$ to $\mathrm{id}_D$; under a chosen homotopy equivalence $D[h^{-1}]\simeq\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ it is homotopic to the identity map of the rank-one endomorphism complex, so it is a homotopy equivalence by [F2]. The reverse evaluation maps are the graded evaluations $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(c)$ on the finite-free tensor-Hom identifications, with the standard Hom differential $d\phi=-(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi d$. They are chain maps because the two terms in $d(\phi\otimes c)$ evaluate to $-(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi(dc)$ and $+(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi(dc)$. For the reduced evaluation square choose a separate module-linear homotopy $\ell$ on $\bar C=C\otimes\mathbb F_2$ satisfying $gf-\mathrm{id}_{\bar C}=d\ell+\ell d$; the homotopy $H$ above acts on $\bar D$ and is not used here. Under the graded flip to the dual-first tensor order, the two reduced evaluation composites are $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(c)$ and $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(gf(c))$, so the reduced square commutes up to $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(\ell(c))$ (over $\mathbb F_2$ the Koszul signs are one), and after localization evaluation identifies with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R[h^{-1}]}(\mathbb R[h^{-1}],\mathbb R[h^{-1}])\to\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$, an isomorphism. Hence the two evaluation maps are local maps in both directions, proving $T\otimes T^*$ locally equivalent to the unknot triple and $T^*$ is an inverse. Finite tensor-Hom associativity, the graded flip, and the unknot's identity endomorphism give associativity, commutativity and the unit, so local-equivalence classes form an abelian group.

By [F4] the domain is the smooth concordance group. By [F3], [F5] and [F6], every prescribed based knot diagram has its LEO triple, and arbitrary based presentations of the same oriented knot are related by marked odd and BN chain homotopy equivalences with compatible reduced squares. The connected-sum chain identifications of [F8] carry the knot triple of $K\#K'$ to the shifted tensor product of the two knot triples, and their reduced comparison is the tensor of the statewise comparisons. The odd signs are balanced for the marked right actions, and the BN vertex sign accounts for the normalized cochain tensor differential, as computed in that supplier. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented knot diagram with ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ and a marked point $p$ away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

The square condition is that the sum of the two signed saddle composites around each two-dimensional cube face is zero. An edge sign function satisfying it is called square-compatible; existence and invariance require separate proofs.

Let $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, with $\deg_q(h)=\deg_q(X)=-2$. Its Frobenius structure has unit $\eta(1)=1$, counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, quotient-ring multiplication, and comultiplication
$$ \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h\,1\otimes1,\qquad \Delta(X)=X\otimes X. $$
Applying these operations to the same normalized cube gives the Bar–Natan cochain complex $C_h(D)$, with circle labels $1,X$ of quantum degrees $1,-1$ and the same normalized state shifts; it is a complex of free $\mathbb R$-modules, and the marked circle acts by multiplication by $X$.

Put $\mathbb B=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)=\mathbb R/(2,h)$. Modulo $2$, the odd exterior basis vector $C_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge C_{i_r}$ corresponds to the even tensor state labeling the selected circles $C_{i_j}$ by $X$ and all other circles by $1$. This statewise bijection defines the candidate comparison $f_D:C_o(D)\otimes\mathbb F_2\to C_h(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B$ after setting $h=0$.

A **local even–odd (LEO) triple** is a triple $(C,D,f)$ consisting of a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $C$ free over $\mathbb A$, a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $D$ free over $\mathbb R$, and a bigraded $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy equivalence
$$ f:C\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_2\longrightarrow D\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B, \qquad \mathbb B=\mathbb R/(2,h)=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2), $$
such that $D[h^{-1}]$ is chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ to one free rank-one module supported in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree. For a based knot diagram the intended candidate is $(C_o(D),C_h(D),f_D)$, where $f_D$ identifies the reduced edge maps modulo $2$ and $h$; its satisfaction of the homotopy and localization conditions is a separate theorem.

A local map $(C,D,f)\to(C',D',f')$ is a pair of bigraded module chain maps $\alpha:C\to C'$ and $\beta:D\to D'$ such that $\beta[h^{-1}]$ is a chain homotopy equivalence and the square induced by $f,f',\alpha,\beta$ after quotienting by $(2,h)$ commutes up to an $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy. Two LEO triples are locally equivalent when there is a local map in each direction.
