Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every finite regular based oriented knot diagram, the odd exterior-algebra cube admits a square-compatible edge assignment and defines a bigraded cochain complex; its mod-2 reduction is chain homotopy equivalent as a marked $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-complex to the Bar–Natan complex reduced modulo $(2,h)$. After inverting $h$, the Bar–Natan complex is chain homotopy equivalent to one free rank-one module in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree over the localized coefficient algebra. Based diagram changes preserve the odd complex up to chain homotopy equivalence, and pointed connected sums give the chain-level tensor product over $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ for the odd complex and over $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$ for the Bar–Natan complex, in each case with the quantum shift $\{-1\}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The set of smooth oriented knot concordance classes in the standard three-sphere is an abelian group under connected sum, with identity the standard unknot and inverse of $[K]$ represented by the reverse mirror $K^\dagger$. Separately, the set of locally flat topological oriented knot concordance classes is an abelian group under connected sum, with the same identity and inverse convention.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let a finite oriented based regular link diagram, with its ordered crossing disks and crossing arrows, lie on an oriented two-sphere. Choose any two orientation-preserving planar coordinate presentations whose omitted points miss the diagram and all crossing disks. Transport the diagram, crossing arrows, over/under information and mark by these coordinates; keep the same crossing order. Circle relabelling gives grading-preserving marked-module chain isomorphisms between their integral odd complexes with transported full admissible edge signs, and between their integral Bar–Natan complexes. In particular the full odd face prescription, including zero-composite faces, is unchanged by the choice of omitted point.

For independently chosen edge assignments satisfying that full prescription, compose the odd relabelling with vertexwise signs. The resulting odd and Bar–Natan isomorphisms have inverse maps, are respectively right linear over $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, and give a strictly commuting square under the statewise reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$. Their inverses give the inverse square. Whenever the endpoint triples satisfy the LEO hypotheses, these maps therefore give local maps in both directions; this applies in particular to knot triples once their separate foundations have been established. The Bar–Natan maps are already chain isomorphisms before localization. The construction is finite and requires no choice axiom. This assertion concerns recharting the same spherical diagram, not transporting a mark through a crossing of a fixed planar diagram.

Assume countable choice. Every prescribed finite regular oriented knot diagram with a specified marked point away from its crossings admits a compatible long endpoint presentation by finitely many planar isotopies and one orientation-preserving spherical rotation recharting. All crossing labels, crossing arrows if specified, strand orientations, over/under data and the mark are transported. No crossing is created, removed, or passed through the mark. The final planar diagram has a round disk containing every crossing and all of the diagram except a single crossing-free exterior closing arc carrying the mark; the disk boundary meets the diagram transversely in exactly two points. A neighborhood of that arc can be used as the protected marked neighborhood in a long-tangle movie.

The recharting omits a point in a face adjacent to the marked germ. Its spherical rotation extends by an explicit orientation-preserving linear map of $S^3$, and the planar normalizations have actual spatial coordinate lifts. Thus the construction records an orientation-preserving spatial identification of the represented marked endpoint knot, rather than declaring its coordinate identifications to be identities. A representative can be chosen with the exterior arc at constant projection height and with product collars at its two cut points. This is a geometric existence assertion. It asserts neither a purely planar protected Reidemeister comparison nor an algebraic invariance theorem. The construction uses only finite selections and explicit maps, so in fact introduces no choice beyond the stated branch.

Assume countable choice. Let $F:S^1\times[0,1]\to S^3$ be a smooth isotopy of oriented knots, stationary in end collars, with a specified marked source point. Suppose its two endpoint diagrams are regular compatible long presentations with the same standard oriented exterior marked arc, parametrized identically on a neighborhood of that point. Use the corresponding spatial endpoint coordinates, in which this common marked arc is a standard small round arc through the stereographic point at infinity; its puncture is closed in the planar diagrams by the same standard exterior arc. Then these prescribed endpoint diagrams are related by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented R1, R2 and R3 moves, whose closed support disks miss the mark. The marked neighborhood remains fixed. There are no births, saddles or deaths. The movie represents the given marked isotopy up to a spatial coordinate family equal to the identity in both end collars and a small isotopy relative those collars.

Here compatible long endpoints include the displayed common oriented arc and its spatial coordinate identifications. This statement does not silently identify arbitrary physical endpoint coordinates. Spherical endpoint recharting may first be used to choose such common compatible presentations; no algebraic invariance of that recharting or of these movies is asserted here.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented collared embedded annulus from a knot $K_0$ to a knot $K_1$. Let $\gamma\subset S$ be a smooth properly embedded arc joining their specified marked points and equal to their vertical marked intervals in smaller end collars. There exist based regular diagrams representing these endpoint knots and a finite oriented movie between them, consisting of planar isotopies, R1, R2, R3, births, saddles and deaths, with a marked point in every frame. The marked track is strictly increasing in height, never dies, never lies at a diagram crossing, and misses the closed support disks of every exceptional move. Every regular interval also keeps a neighborhood of the mark fixed in its chosen diagram coordinates.

More precisely, first an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller end collars carries the given marked surface to one with monotone marked arc. A smooth level-preserving change of spatial coordinates then puts a neighborhood of that arc into a fixed exterior closing-arc position. The movie trace, transported back by those same coordinates, is ambient isotopic to the original marked $S$ relative to the smaller end collars. Its endpoint diagrams and their marked parametrizations use the corresponding endpoint coordinate identifications. One may retain prescribed endpoint diagrams already in this compatible long-tangle presentation. The conclusion does not assert a based Reidemeister sequence between arbitrary prescribed planar endpoint diagrams or between arbitrary basepoint presentations, and asserts no movie-independence theorem for algebraic maps.

Let a finite oriented link-cobordism movie carry a marked point continuously through its regular levels, with its trace disjoint from all elementary move disks, and with the marked component never dying. Use the odd cubes with the prescribed full face signs and the integral Bar–Natan cubes over $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$. This movie admits an integral odd map, linear for the marked right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action, and an integral marked $\mathbb R$-linear Bar–Natan map. They have cohomological degree zero and quantum degree the Euler characteristic of the movie, and their reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ agree under the statewise comparison. For a connected oriented concordance between knots the localized Bar–Natan map is a chain homotopy equivalence over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$. A localized knot complex retracts over that ring onto one free rank-one module in cohomological degree zero and odd quantum parity. All these statements concern the supplied movie; no independence from its presentation is asserted. The finite algebraic constructions use no choice axiom.

Let two finite based knot diagrams be joined along their marked arcs in a planar pointed connected-sum diagram, without new crossings. The odd complexes admit a normalized bigraded right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain isomorphism
$$ C_o(D_1)\otimes_{\mathbb A}C_o(D_2)\{-1\}\ \cong\ C_o(D_1\#D_2), $$
and the Bar–Natan complexes admit the corresponding marked $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$-linear chain isomorphism. In the odd case the induced signs realize the full prescribed face products, so admissible sign comparison applies, including zero-composite faces. The two isomorphisms agree after reduction modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ under the statewise comparison. Their construction is finite and choice-free.

Thus local equivalence is an equivalence relation.

The graded symmetry $u\otimes v\mapsto(-1)^{|u||v|}v\otimes u$ gives commutativity, and the unknot triple is the unit because its complexes are $\mathbb A\{1\}$ and $\mathbb R\{1\}$.

By [F4] the domain is the smooth concordance group. By [F3], [F5] and [F6], every prescribed based knot diagram has its LEO triple, and arbitrary based presentations of the same oriented knot are related by marked odd and BN chain homotopy equivalences with compatible reduced squares. In particular those pairs are local maps in both directions, so they define the same local-equivalence class. The full foundations proof constructs the finite common endpoint model before using the protected R-only comparison; no assertion that a planar move can pass a mark through a crossing is assumed. Thus the assignment is independent of the diagram and basepoint presentation.

Let two knots be smoothly concordant. Their arbitrary prescribed based endpoint diagrams are first normalized by [F6], with the spherical marked isomorphisms of [F5]. The annulus has a proper marked arc joining the boundary marks. The relative annulus movie of [F7], with the common endpoint-strip comparison proved in the foundations argument, supplies a protected finite movie. The integral odd map is right $\mathbb A$-linear; the BN map is right $\mathbb R$-linear. Their reductions agree under the statewise comparison, and the BN composite becomes a marked-ring chain homotopy equivalence after inverting $h$. The annulus has Euler characteristic zero, so these maps preserve both gradings. Compose them with the actual endpoint isomorphisms to obtain a local map between the original triples; the reverse annulus yields a local map in the other direction. Hence concordant knots have the same local-equivalence class. Individual Morse maps need not be localized equivalences; [F7] proves the required assertion for the entire connected concordance composite. No odd movie-independence theorem is used.

The connected-sum chain identifications of [F8] carry the knot triple of $K\#K'$ to the shifted tensor product of the two knot triples, and their reduced comparison is the tensor of the statewise comparisons. The odd signs are balanced for the marked right actions, and the BN vertex sign accounts for the normalized cochain tensor differential, as computed in that supplier. The arbitrary representative comparison from step 4.1 permits these identifications to be made in convenient planar pointed-sum presentations without restricting the original endpoints. Thus the class of $K\#K'$ is the product of the classes of $K$ and $K'$. The unknot goes to the unit triple of step 2.1. By [F4] the reverse mirror is the inverse of $K$ in the smooth concordance group, so the just-proved tensor identity and concordance invariance send it to the inverse class in the target group of step 3.1. Consequently the assignment is a well-defined homomorphism with the entire asserted scope.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented knot $K$, let $V_K$ be its two-dimensional rational Lee homology with the diagram-independent induced decreasing quantum filtration $F^pV_K$. For a nonzero class $x\in V_K$, define its filtration level by
$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$
Set
$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a connected compact oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with product collars and oriented boundary $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$ for oriented knots $K_0,K_1$ in the standard three-sphere. A **finite movie** for $S$ is a finite ordered sequence of regular-level link diagrams whose changes are planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves, births, saddles or deaths. Such a movie defines a map on rational Lee homology that preserves the induced decreasing filtration with degree $\chi(S)=-2g$. The map is an isomorphism; consequently
$$
|s(K_1)-s(K_0)|\le 2g.
$$

Assume countable choice. Let $F\subset B^4\subset\mathbb R^4$ be a compact connected oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with its supplied smooth boundary collar and oriented boundary the knot $K\subset S^3$. There is an orientation-preserving ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi:B^4\to B^4$ equal to the identity on a neighborhood of the outer boundary, and $0<\varepsilon<1$, such that $\Psi(F)\cap B^4_\varepsilon$ is exactly a flat two-disk in a plane through $0$. The surface $\Psi(F)\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon$, in the explicitly round shell $B^4\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon\cong S^3\times[0,1]$, is a connected smooth oriented knot cobordism between $K$ and a standard unknot, with genus $g$ and Euler characteristic $-2g$. Both boundary components have product collars in a shell identification fixing $K$ and the inner sphere. The ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi$ fixes a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar; the shell coordinates may be adjusted there to make that surface collar a product. No assertion about the complement of an arbitrary embedded four-ball is used.

derivations.claim: For the standard crossingless unknot diagram, the Lee complex is the one-term vector space $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$ with basis $1,X$ in quantum degrees $1,-1$ and zero differential. Its induced filtration levels are therefore $s_{\max}(U)=1$ and $s_{\min}(U)=-1$, so [F2] gives $s(U)=0$.

Let $F\subset B^4$ be any connected smooth orientable proper spanning surface of genus $g$ with boundary $K$. Apply [F4] under the countable-choice hypothesis [A1]. It moves and flattens a small interior surface disk by ambient diffeomorphisms fixed on a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar, then removes an actual concentric round ball. The remaining round shell is explicitly $S^3\times I$, with unchanged boundary knot $K$, an inner standard unknot and product collars. Its surface is connected of the same genus $g$ and has Euler characteristic $-2g$; reverse its direction if needed. This uses neither a slice-only Statement for a positive-genus surface nor a claim about arbitrary embedded four-ball complements.

Apply the Lee cobordism construction to this surface and to its reverse. By [F3], each map is a filtered isomorphism of degree $-2g$. Choose a nonzero class of maximal level in $V_K$; its image is nonzero in $V_U$ and has level at least $s_{\max}(K)-2g$, which is at most $s_{\max}(U)=1$. Hence $s_{\max}(K)\le1+2g$ and $s(K)\le2g$. Apply the reverse map to a nonzero class of maximal level in $V_U$: its nonzero image in $V_K$ has level at least $1-2g$, so $s_{\max}(K)\ge1-2g$ and $s(K)\ge-2g$.

Under [A1], [F1] supplies a nonempty set of smooth spanning-surface genera with a least element. Minimize $g$ over $F$ in step 1.2. Step 2.1 then gives the asserted inequality. This gives the inequality in the Statement.

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot admitting a finite regular diagram $D$ with $n$ positive crossings and no negative crossings, and let $k$ be the number of circles in its oriented resolution. Then Rasmussen’s invariant satisfies
$$
s(K)=n-k+1.
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice.

Let $K^\dagger$ be the reverse mirror of an oriented knot $K$. Then
$$
s(K^\dagger)=-s(K).
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil with two full twists in the clasp, using the twist convention of Hedden and Ording. The normalized knot Floer threshold and Rasmussen invariant satisfy
$$\tau(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=0,\qquad s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets (Finite, countably infinite, countable, uncountable) has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil in the Hedden–Ording twist convention, with companion-annulus framing two. Equivalently, start with the three-crossing positive trefoil blackboard parallel, add one negative full annulus twist, and attach the positive clasp as in the admitted sixteen-crossing code. Then
$$s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil with two full twists in the clasp, using the twist convention of Hedden and Ording. The normalized knot Floer threshold and Rasmussen invariant satisfy
$$\tau(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=0,\qquad s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere,
$$
|s(K)|\le 2g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K),
$$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surface in the standard four-ball with oriented boundary $K$.

derivations.claim: Under [A1], the crossingless unknot complex has one cohomological degree and basis $1,X$ in quantum degrees $1,-1$, so its two filtration levels are $1,-1$. The definition $s=s_{\max}-1=s_{\min}+1$ gives $s(U)=0$.
The standard positive trefoil diagram has $n=3$ crossings and $k=2$ circles in its oriented resolution. Applying [F2] gives $s(T_{2,3})=3-2+1=2$. By [F3], its reverse mirror has value $-2$.

The trefoil Seifert construction from the given diagram starts with two disks and attaches three bands, so its connected orientable surface has Euler characteristic $2-3=-1$ and one boundary component. The identity $\chi=1-2g$ gives genus $1$. Push its interior into a collar of the boundary three-sphere in the four-ball, using a height function that vanishes only on the boundary knot; its graph is still an embedded orientable surface with the same boundary and genus. Thus [F5] gives $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(T_{2,3})\le1$. The bound in [F6] gives $2=|s(T_{2,3})|\le2g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(T_{2,3})$, so its smooth four-ball genus is $1$.

Apply the joint value lemma [F4] to the actual positive-clasped double with two full twists. Its diagram and zero-longitude convention are exactly those stipulated here, so it gives $s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2$ and $\tau(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=0$. Together with the unknot and trefoil calculations and the smooth genus computation above, these are every value asserted in the Example.

Curves from different systems intersect transversely in finitely many points. Each component of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\alpha$ and of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\beta$ contains exactly one $w$-point and exactly one $z$-point. The diagram also includes trivial arc systems in the two handlebodies: the $\alpha$-arcs join $w_i$ to $z_i$, and the $\beta$-arcs join $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$, with indices modulo $k$. Each system is disjoint from its compression disks and is simultaneously boundary parallel: its arcs cobound pairwise disjoint embedded disks with arcs in the corresponding components of the attaching-system complement on $\Sigma$. Thus each ball obtained by compression contains one unknotted arc. Together the arcs form an oriented knot, oriented from $w_i$ to $z_i$ in $U_{\alpha}$ and from $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$ in $U_{\beta}$. The diagram is **compatible with $K$** when this knot is orientation-preservingly ambient isotopic to $K$. For a grid diagram, compatibility uses the row and column orientation fixed in the grid definition, with $w$-points at $O$ and $z$-points at $X$. Equivalently one may specify the surface isomorphism together with its compatible collared extensions over both handlebodies carrying those arcs. The attaching systems are carried as systems; reordering their curve factors induces the corresponding product identification. Comparisons also allow **arc normalizations in the fixed splitting**: a smooth isotopy of the represented oriented knot, supported near the ordered marks and fixing each mark, during which every open connecting arc stays in its original handlebody and the two simultaneous boundary-parallel witness systems are retained or replaced by embedded witnesses for those same arcs. The surface, attaching curves, marked points and compression disks stay fixed. Analytic and assigned grading data depending on the fixed surface diagram can be kept identical; the corresponding generator and disk-count identification is then the identity. Such a comparison transports the represented oriented knot and any specified Seifert surface as well. For analytic data, it transports $j$, the surface area form, all chosen divisor neighborhoods and $J_t$ by the induced symmetric-product diffeomorphism. The comparison maps on generators and disk classes are their pushforwards under this map; compatibility with the count differential is a mathematical property to be proved. No identity action is part of this convention, even when the ambient diffeomorphism is isotopic to the identity.

Let $q:\Sigma^m\to\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ be the quotient map. The product tori are the images $\mathbb T_{\alpha}=q(\alpha_1\times\cdots\times\alpha_m)$ and $\mathbb T_{\beta}=q(\beta_1\times\cdots\times\beta_m)$. Their intersection points are the generators. Its domain is the integral two-chain of complementary regions with coefficients equal to local multiplicities. Write $n_{w_i}(\phi)$ and $n_{z_i}(\phi)$ for its local multiplicities at the marked points. An almost complex structure $J$ on $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ is a smooth endomorphism of the tangent bundle with $J^2=-1$. Fix a complex structure $j$ and an area form on $\Sigma$. The path is a sufficiently small perturbation in this class. For $m=0$ the symmetric product is a point. Local multiplicities are intersection numbers with these divisors; positivity is a mathematical property to be proved, not an additional choice of disk counts. statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix an actual balanced multipointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with $k\ge1$ cyclically ordered mark pairs, $m=h+k-1$, transverse attaching systems and complete compression disks cutting the two handlebodies into $k$ balls. Broad auxiliary proper disk witnesses are permitted. Label the cut components by $A_i$ containing $w_i,z_i$ and $B_i$ containing $w_i,z_{i+1}$, cyclically.

There is a choice of integrable surface background, protected nearly symmetric geometry, common exact generator charts and ONE smooth tame path constant on genuine positive time collars, with no nonconstant strip of index at most zero, for which every actual nonconstant strip of index one or two is regular and there are finitely many index-one translation orbits across ALL generators, realized classes and nonnegative $w,z$ vectors. No $n_z=0$ restriction is imposed. Its endpoint unit boundary disks are regular and finite at every generator. Their mod-two counts are one for each $A_i,B_i$ when $k\ge2$, and zero for the single alpha and beta components when $k=1$; in the latter case unit spheres through the generators are excluded as in the singly pointed construction.

Let $C$ be the free module on the finite generator set over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$. The ACTUAL differential
$$d x=\sum_{y,\,[u]\in\widehat{\mathcal M}_1(x,y)}U_1^{n_{w_1}(u)}\cdots U_k^{n_{w_k}(u)}\,y$$
counts all the above index-one orbits, including every positive $z$ multiplicity. It is a finite polynomial matrix, $d^2=0$, and it preserves the relative Alexander filtration with each $U_i$ lowering filtration by one. Identifying or localizing variables by any ring homomorphism preserves this identity.

For $k\ge2$, retaining separate $V_i$ weights for $z_i$ gives the actual full-marked curvature identity
$$D^2=\left(\sum_{i=1}^kU_i(V_i+V_{i+1})\right)I.$$
For $k=1$ the corresponding full-marked $D$ has $D^2=0$ by the zero unit counts. These are chosen-data analytic count identities. Comparison to other paths or diagrams, absolute gradings, analytic/combinatorial identification and Floer invariance are not input or conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice. Use the actual balanced $S^3$ knot data with $k\ge1$ and THE chosen surface complex structure and genuine constant-collar path constructed in the corresponding multipointed or singly pointed full-marked low-index count theorem, whose construction excludes every nonconstant strip of index at most zero as well as giving full-marked index-one and index-two regularity and finite counts. For $k=1$ this is the sphere-avoiding path from the singly pointed theorem. Label the individual cut components so $A_i$ contains $w_i,z_i$ and $B_i$ contains $w_i,z_{i+1}$, with cyclic indices.

For fixed generators $x,y$ and nonnegative integer vectors $W,Z$, let $\widehat{\mathcal M}_2(x,y;W,Z)$ consist of ALL actual index-two strips with these ends and marked-degree vectors, modulo longitudinal translation, across all realized Whitney classes. This is a Hausdorff second-countable topological one-manifold. It has a compactification as a compact one-manifold with finite boundary, whose boundary points are exactly:

1. Ordered pairs of actual rigid index-one strip orbits with matched intermediate generator and marked vectors summing to $W,Z$.
2. When $x=y$, the actual unit $A_i$ or $B_i$ boundary-disk orbits with boundary node value $x$ and the prescribed marked vector, attached to the constant generator strip.

Each point has the actual exhaustive one-sided gluing collar of its respective type. No extra boundary points occur, and no differentiability at a prescribed compactifying parameter is asserted.

Let $a_i(x),b_i(x)\in\mathbb F_2$ be the actual finite node-fixed affine-orbit counts of the $A_i,B_i$ disks at $x$. On the free module generated by the generators over $R=\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k,V_1,\ldots,V_k]$, define $D$ by the actual finite rigid-strip counts with weight $U^{n_w}V^{n_z}$. Then
$$D^2x=\left(\sum_{i=1}^k a_i(x)U_iV_i+\sum_{i=1}^k b_i(x)U_iV_{i+1}\right)x.$$
Setting every $V_i=1$ gives the actual full filtered minus count operator $d$ and
$$d^2x=\left(\sum_{i=1}^k(a_i(x)+b_i(x))U_i\right)x.$$
For $k=1$ the actual singly pointed unit-disk theorem supplies $a_1(x)=b_1(x)=0$, and hence $D^2=d^2=0$. For $k\ge2$ the counts $a_i,b_i$ are not evaluated here, so square-zero in that case and unit disk count one are not concluded. Invariance and absolute normalization are not asserted. The full marked compactification and curvature identity retain the actual remaining multipointed boundary counts explicitly.

Assume Countable Choice. $$q(\mathcal E(x,v))=q(x)+dq_xv$$
for all sufficiently small $v$. Derivatives of every fixed order of this addition and its inverse are uniformly bounded on smaller neighborhoods in finite coordinate covers. This is a genuine finite-dimensional boundary-preserving local addition, not an assumption about a Sobolev map space.

Witness parametrizations can be chosen for the finite disk families. This category convention does not require the knot arcs to meet the Heegaard surface transversely: tangential smooth crossings remain permitted.

A **handlebody** is a compact three-manifold that is a regular neighborhood of a finite connected graph. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

statement.

Let $C$ and $D$ be finite integer-filtered chain complexes over $\mathbb F_2$, each with total homology isomorphic to $\mathbb F_2$. A filtered chain homotopy equivalence consists of filtration-preserving chain maps $f:C\to D$ and $g:D\to C$ such that $gf$ and $fg$ are chain homotopic to the respective identity maps by homotopies that preserve every filtration level. Then $\tau(C)=\tau(D)$.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, let $F$ be a compact connected oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H_0,\mathcal H_1$ be admissible multipointed Heegaard diagrams for $K$. For $i=0,1$, the diagram $\mathcal H_i$ has a closed genus-$h_i$ Heegaard surface and $m_i=h_i+k_i-1$ curves in each attaching system, with $k_i$ ordered $w$-points and $k_i$ ordered $z$-points; each component of either attaching-system complement contains one point of each type, and the connecting arcs represent $K$. A curve isotopy is an isotopy of one attaching curve through embedded curves in its attaching system, disjoint from the other attaching curves and all marked points. A handleslide replaces one attaching curve by its band sum with another curve in the same attaching system, along an embedded arc disjoint from the other attaching curves and the marked points. A Heegaard stabilization forms connected sum with the genus-one splitting of $S^3$ in a disk disjoint from all curves, marked points, and knot arcs; it raises the genus by one and leaves $k$ fixed. A basepoint-pair (index-zero/three) stabilization keeps the genus fixed and adds one curve to each system and one $w,z$ pair along the represented knot. Its inverse removes the following elementary configuration, after relabeling the cyclic pairs: curves $\alpha_0,\beta_0$ bound disks $A_0,B_0$ on the surface, are disjoint from every opposite-system curve except each other, and intersect transversely in two points; $A_0\cap B_0$ is a bigon containing just $w_0$, while $A_0\setminus B_0$ contains just $z_0$ and $B_0\setminus A_0$ contains the next $z$-point along the cyclic pairing. Remove $\alpha_0,\beta_0,w_0,z_0$ and concatenate the adjacent trivial knot arcs. The surviving marked points stay fixed. Thus the move inserts a pair along an existing knot arc rather than adjoining an isolated marked component in an empty disk. Both descriptions include the simultaneous boundary-parallel arc systems and require the stated one-$w$, one-$z$ condition in each attaching complement. Destabilizations are the respective inverse moves. Comparisons may apply the orientation-preserving diagram isomorphisms of the pointed-data definition, carrying the ordered marked points, attaching systems and simultaneous boundary-parallel arcs, before or after the listed geometric moves. Their complex identifications are induced by pushforward of generators, disk classes and almost complex data, rather than by assuming an isotopy acts as the identity. Comparisons also allow the fixed-splitting arc normalizations in that definition before or after the listed moves, retaining the simultaneous bridge witnesses and all ordered marks. They leave the surface attaching and analytic data fixed, so their identification of the actual count operators is the identity; they do not assert a diffeomorphism of a tangential and transverse surface-knot pair. With these identifications, any two such diagrams are related by a finite sequence of the listed moves through admissible multipointed diagrams, preserving the represented oriented knot.

For a diagram with $j$ basepoint pairs, regard its full filtered minus complex as a complex over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by restriction of scalars along $U\mapsto U_i$ for any one chosen basepoint variable. The resulting complexes of $\mathcal H_0$ and $\mathcal H_1$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb F_2[U]$, preserving relative Maslov grading and Alexander filtration, even when the diagrams have different numbers of basepoint pairs. The choice of the single variable action does not affect this type. Restriction retains the independent variables in the chain module; it is different from quotienting by $U_1=\cdots=U_j$. The latter ordinary quotient is the fully collapsed complex and has filtered chain homotopy type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(j-1)}$, where $V$ has zero differential and bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$. Equivalently, a basepoint stabilization before quotienting is modeled by the cone of $U_{j+1}+U_i$ on the polynomial extension of the old complex; after the simultaneous quotient this is a zero-map cone and contributes the displayed extra factor.

For an admissible doubly-pointed diagram $\mathcal H_1$ for $(K,F)$, define $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ to be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from its full filtered minus complex by quotienting by its sole variable $U$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ use the Alexander grading
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned by the pointed Heegaard construction from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, and $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood of $K$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached so that this longitude bounds it (zero-framed surgery). The vector-field representative is extended across small balls around the critical points, and its first Chern class is the Chern class of the orthogonal oriented plane field. Use the absolute Maslov normalization in which the unique generator of $\widehat{HF}(S^3)$ has degree zero.

For a diagram $\mathcal H$ with $j$ basepoint pairs, let $\widetilde C(\mathcal H)$ be the Alexander-associated-graded complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from its full filtered minus complex by setting every $U_i=0$; its differential therefore counts only classes with all $n_{w_i}=n_{z_i}=0$. Its homology is $\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(j-1)}$, where $V=\mathbb F_2\langle v_0,v_1\rangle$ has bidegrees $(M,A)(v_0)=(0,0)$ and $(M,A)(v_1)=(-1,-1)$.

A cyclic permutation changes the planar cut of the toroidal grid by moving the first row or column to the last. A row commutation exchanges consecutive rows whose closed horizontal marking intervals are disjoint or strictly nested; a column commutation uses the same condition on vertical marking intervals. citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets (Finite, countably infinite, countable, uncountable) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice. Let $K_0,K_1\subset S^3$ be smooth oriented knots. A smooth oriented knot cobordism from $K_0$ to $K_1$ is a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ whose boundary is $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$, with product collars at both ends. A **generic movie** for $\Sigma$ is obtained by choosing a generic projection of the slices $S^3\times\{t\}$ to the plane and a Morse height function on $\Sigma$, then recording the oriented link diagram at each regular level. Intermediate regular levels may be links with any finite number of components. After choosing the projection and height generically, the finitely many exceptional levels are isolated and distinct: between them the diagrams change by planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move, and at them the surface height has one nondegenerate minimum (a birth), one nondegenerate maximum (a death), or one index-one critical point (a saddle band move). A movie includes its ordered list of frames and these elementary changes; no claim that two movies of the same cobordism are equivalent is part of this definition.

Assume countable choice. Fix $\infty\in S^3$, put $A=\{\infty\}\times[0,1]$, and identify its complement with $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$. Let $S_0,S_1$ be compact smooth oriented link cobordisms disjoint from $A$, with the same fixed boundary parametrizations and product collars. If they are ambient isotopic in $S^3\times[0,1]$ relative to those collars, then their comparison factors into finitely many ambient isotopies supported in the Euclidean complement and finitely many local sheet passages through $A$. Each sheet passage occurs at a regular surface-height point and gives the sweep-around move: in planar movies, a closing arc for a one-interval tangle travels over the tangle to the opposite side and returns underneath, or the inverse, retaining its orientation. All end collars remain fixed. No assertion that a sweep-around is generated by the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito moves, or that any homology map respects it, is made.

Assume countable choice. Let two finite generic planar movies represent compact smooth oriented surfaces in $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$, with the same parametrized boundary and product collars. If their embedded surfaces are ambient isotopic with compact support relative to those collars, then the two movies are related by a finite sequence of the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito local types, distant interchanges of disjoint elementary movie events, and planar isotopies. All orientations and omitted-coordinate crossing orders are retained. This statement concerns Euclidean isotopies; it supplies no sweep-around relation.

Use coordinates $(x,y,z,t)$ on Euclidean space-time, with projection $(x,y,z,t)\mapsto(x,y,t)$; $z$ records the crossing order. A local movie move replaces the movies on the two sides of an isolated value $\lambda=0$ in a one-parameter deformation of a projected surface, with the surface and its collars unchanged outside the indicated region. Coordinates and cutoffs are chosen so the two movies have identical boundary frames. The following list specifies the fifteen Carter–Saito types, with their usual numbering. Include both directions, reflections, all compatible strand orientations, and every crossing order allowed by distinct $z$-coordinates. The quadratic and higher-order formulas specify the local topological models; sufficiently small perturbations with the same nonzero derivative signs give the same type.

| Type | Local change of the movie |
|---|---|
| MM1, MM2 | A pair of inverse R1 events is created or removed. In regular-height source coordinates $(v,t)$ the projected curve has local form $(v^2,(t^2-\lambda)v+c v^3)$, $c\ne0$; the two signs of $c$ relative to the quadratic term give the two types. |
| MM3, MM4 | A pair of inverse R2 events is created or removed. After the two projected branches are made graphs, their normal difference is $x^2+t^2-\lambda$ or $x^2-t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM5 | A pair of inverse R3 events is created or removed. With the intersection of two strands continued as the reference point, the signed displacement of the third strand is $t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM6 | An R3 event passes an R2 event: at the projected triple point exactly two projected tangents become parallel, with nonzero quadratic contact and nonzero relative deformation velocity. |
| MM7 | An R2 event meets a branch endpoint of the double-curve locus of an R1 picture. In projected coordinates use $(v^2,tv+\lambda v^3+v^5)$; its double pairs have $r=v^2\ge0$ and $t=-\lambda r-r^2$, so a critical point of the double-curve height enters or leaves through $r=0$. |
| MM8 | A third strand passes the branch point of an R1 picture; superpose a transverse strand on the ordinary cusp unfolding and move its displacement across zero. |
| MM9 | Two R2 critical levels merge and disappear, or are created, at a cubic inflection of the double curve: the branch-difference model is $x^3+\lambda x-t$. |
| MM10 | Four sheets meet at one projected point, with distinct omitted heights. Resolving the quadruple point in the two deformation directions gives the tetrahedral pair of R3 movies. |
| MM11 | A cancelling pair of surface Morse critical points is born or dies. The surface-height model is $u^2+v^3-\lambda v$, allowing both signs of the nondegenerate square and time reversal. |
| MM12 | At an extremum of surface height the projection of its tangent plane has rank one. A local embedded model is $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2+v^2)$; the two movies interchange the extremum with its adjacent R1 picture. |
| MM13 | The corresponding interaction at a saddle, with embedded model $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2-v^2)$. |
| MM14 | A projected strand passes a surface minimum or maximum: superpose an independently displaced regular sheet on the extremum picture. |
| MM15 | The corresponding projected strand passage across a saddle band. |

A **distant interchange** exchanges the order of two elementary movie events with disjoint spatial supports, including Reidemeister events and Morse events; it is not restricted to two critical points of the smooth surface-height function. A planar isotopy of a whole movie and the insertion or removal of stationary frames do not count as additional local types. Sweep-around is a separate spherical operation, absent from this Euclidean list.

derivations.claim: Use the actual smooth traced realizations of the two planar movies, with their prescribed endpoint realizations and collars. These lie in the standard spatial chart $S^3\setminus\{\infty\}$; by [F1] and the hypothesis, their oriented traces have the specified spherical isotopy relative to those collars. Apply [F2]. The comparison is a finite sequence of Euclidean isotopies and isolated sweep-around events, with the same parametrized boundary. At the intermediate cuts choose generic movies fixed on the retained collars; the same finite-jet construction in [F3] applies with these cuts protected.

On each Euclidean isotopy interval, [F3] replaces its comparison by finitely many of the fifteen local moves, distant interchanges and planar isotopies. All hidden-coordinate height orders and orientations are preserved. At each missing-arc passage retain the sweep-around supplied by [F2]; it is not silently replaced by a Euclidean move. The two boundary movies of each interval match those at the adjacent pieces, because the construction fixes the chosen cuts and collars.

Concatenate these finite lists. There are finitely many intervals and passages, so the total list is finite. Every retained frame is a regular frame of a generic traced surface, and every elementary replacement has its stated oriented local trace with the same outside and boundary data. Consequently all intermediate movies have the prescribed parametrized knots and collars. The total sequence starts and ends at the given movies and proves the claimed spherical comparison.

Arbitrarily small smooth Hamiltonian isotopies of the individual families, supported away from all the protected and witness points, give pairwise transverse representatives with NO point on three curves from different families. Their pair intersections are canonically followed through the small isotopies, without birth or death. When the corresponding product tori have common POSITIVE rank $m>0$, no point belongs to three DISTINCT torus labels. At rank zero the empty product tori all equal the point of $\operatorname{Sym}^0\Sigma$; no exclusion of their triple intersection is claimed, and their source-dependent target transport is the identity. The complete disk-cut and based-link data can be transported by the family isotopies; no topology of the underlying handlebodies is changed.

Full-curve periodic-domain lattices and their sublattices generated by pairwise periodic domains transport bijectively by the swept annuli. All coefficients at the original witness and protected points are unchanged. Consequently any strict weak or strong admissibility criterion witnessed by these coefficients is preserved, when its indexing and linear evaluation are transported under this lattice map. Identification of that evaluation with a geometric Spin-c or Fredholm quantity is a separate topological assertion, not part of this lemma.

For an actual boundary-marked polygon source, the relative map spaces with fixed corresponding corner labels are homeomorphic by an actual smooth source-dependent target isotopy. It is the identity near protected incidence divisors and the diagonal and is fixed in the longitudinal coordinate on each far end. This induces bijections on literal continuous relative homotopy classes, without quotienting by a fundamental-group action. No symmetric power of a nonholomorphic surface map is used as a global smooth target map. For smooth fixed-end reference maps the transported actual Fredholm index is unchanged. These are class and admissibility transports, not an equality of holomorphic counts or an isotopy-invariance theorem.

Supply their disjoint compression disks in oriented handlebodies $U_i$, their compatible Morse functions with $k$ index-zero and $m$ index-one critical points, and $k$ distinct points $\mathbf w$ with one in each cut component of every system. Distinct systems meet transversely and finitely. Use the usual product tori in $\operatorname{Sym}^m\Sigma$. Let $W$ be the oriented polygon cobordism obtained from the polygon times $\Sigma$ by attaching $e_i\times U_i$ along $e_i\times\Sigma$, with rounded corners. A realized Whitney polygon is a continuous disk map with these successive torus edges and specified corner generators; no holomorphic representative is assumed.

The finite Morse construction below assigns such a class $u$ a Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s_{\mathbf w}(u)$ on $W$, restricting to the specified Morse labels of its corners. If $u,v$ have the same corners, their domain difference $P=D(u)-D(v)$ has boundary an integral sum of full attaching circles. Capping those circles with the supplied disks along polygon legs gives a class $H(P)\in H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$. With the common source/surface orientations, their Spin-c difference is

where $j:H^2(W,\partial W;\mathbb Z)\to H^2(W;\mathbb Z)$. The sign is fixed by the positive index-one/index-two gradient modification having determinant degree $+2$ on a positive transverse disk.

For a triangle these are the $\alpha\beta$, $\beta\gamma$ and $\alpha\gamma$ pairs. Their capped classes need not be zero individually. Fixed all $w,z$ multiplicities imply this hypothesis without any extra normalization convention.

The construction is compatible with gluing polygons along a common Heegaard boundary. Compatible Spin-c structures on the pieces have the usual extension orbit under the image of $H^1$ of that common boundary in $H^2$ of the glued cobordism; no unique extension is asserted. Along an actual continuous class-preserving family and its actual neck-smoothing, the assigned total Spin-c structure is constant, and the glued pieces recover that total extension, not an arbitrarily chosen member of the orbit. Point-divisor multiplicity vectors at every supplied $w,z$ mark add under these actual gluings. These assertions do not supply an analytic compactification or a gluing existence theorem. For supplied small attaching-curve isotopies away from the marks, transport the compatible Morse data in the actual handlebody collars and supply a continuous transport of the polygon maps. On the unchanged cobordism this carries their Spin-c labels and capped periodic classes, including torsion information. If one witness point in every old region misses the swept curves, all coefficients at those witnesses are unchanged. Hence strict strong admissibility, and the corresponding sector or global weak witness conditions, pass to the transported lattice. No existence of the continuous polygon-map transport is inferred from the mere isotopy of its boundary curves.

The statement does not identify all literal Whitney classes with their domains, divide genus-two classes by a sphere action, assert finiteness of classes with one domain, or supply any analytic count or Maslov-index formula. The point target $m=0$ has only the constant map and the domain conclusion is zero.

On $G$ put $\ell(P)=\langle c_1(\mathfrak s),H(P)\rangle/2$. The values of $\ell$ are integers. Assume the strict strong-admissibility condition

Then the relative-index functional

is strictly positive on every nonzero nonnegative direction in $L$. The nonnegative domains of actual same-corner, same-Spin-c polygons have a finite lower relative-index bound. For every integer $K$, only finitely many such nonnegative integral domains have relative index at most $K$. These statements concern domains, not the number of literal homotopy classes or holomorphic maps with one domain. Thus every nonempty fixed-end strip sector has a lower actual index bound $L_0$ and finitely many nonnegative domains of indices in $[L_0,K]$. For fixed attaching curves, marks and labels these bounds and finite sets are independent of the Cauchy–Riemann coefficients, auxiliary family parameters and source conformal parameters satisfying the same index conventions; they depend only on the finite domain lattice and Chern functional. No uniformity under an unspecified change of attaching curves is asserted.

If every nonzero $P\in G$ with $\ell(P)=0$ has both signs, then at a fixed entire mark vector and any fixed finite set of relative indices there are only finitely many nonnegative domains in the fixed Spin-c sector. For supplied actual strip classes the pair version also holds under the separate weaker condition testing mixed signs only on REALIZED normalized index-zero periodic classes. This proves a finite-domain statement only for supplied actual classes; it neither establishes invariance under moves nor supplies a generator in an intended sector whose generator set is empty. It does not give an unrestricted lower index bound. Any separately supplied uniform positive area bound also bounds every nonnegative component domain and hence its index, by its finite region coefficients.

There is a separate all-Spin-c zero-mark conclusion. If every nonzero formal periodic domain with all $w$ multiplicities zero has both positive and negative coefficients, then for fixed corners and fixed zero $w$ multiplicities there are only finitely many nonnegative domains, without fixing a Spin-c structure or an index. This global multi-periodic hypothesis is not inferred from strong admissibility for one Spin-c structure or from pairwise weak admissibility. No existence or winding construction of either type of diagram is asserted.

Fix a Spin-c structure on the polygon cobordism and use the STRICT all-$w$ normalized strong admissibility condition of the named geometric lattice theorem. Use the same condition for its relevant boundary-pair sectors. The boundary systems have their actual complete $k$-ball cuts, and nearly symmetric geometry has exact constant product-angle generator charts. No $S^3$ or torsion restriction on the intermediate three-manifolds is made.

In the smooth topology, the genuine constant-collar end paths having no nonconstant strip of index at most zero and regularity for every actual index-one strip in the relevant sectors form an open dense subset of the allowed protected end paths. With these paths, compatible coherent source-dependent polygon perturbations can be chosen generically, relative to their faces and any regular parameter endpoints. Their count-dimension-zero total sets are finite, and their count-dimension-one spaces compactify to actual compact one-manifolds. All nonnegative $w,z$ degrees are retained. These conclusions hold for the fixed total Spin-c label, across all its literal realized classes; they also hold for fixed degree vectors or fixed actual classes. The boundary consists exactly of the label-compatible rigid polygon–polygon faces and strip–polygon breakings, with additive marked vectors and actual exhaustive gluing collars. No sphere or one-torus disk bubble occurs in these polygon dimensions. This includes $k=1$.

For triangles the fixed count index is $\mu$, so rigid counts have $\mu=0$ and the chain-map boundary has $\mu=1$. In a generic one-parameter triangle family with fixed regular end data the universal count index is $\mu+1$: the index-minus-one universal counts are finite, and universal index-zero spaces have the parameter endpoints and strip–triangle boundaries. Thus the finite actual counts satisfy the weighted triangle chain-map equation and its auxiliary-data chain homotopy over $\mathbb F_2$. They may be specialized to the two-color ring by sending every $w$ variable to $U$ and every $z$ variable to $V$. No top-generator cycle, handle-map inverse, arbitrary diagram invariance or absolute grading is part of this assertion.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with admissible Heegaard data and regular almost-complex structures for its elementary pieces. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For a piece represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{n_w(\phi)}V^{n_z(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class, and the other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.

derivations.claim: Treat rank zero directly. The target and all empty product tori are one point. The fixed-map operator is the zero map from the zero section space to the zero forcing space; it is onto of index zero. The three-marked source has no conformal parameter or automorphism. Hence its unique map is a regular isolated triangle with all marked degrees zero, in its assigned constant-class Spin-c extension. With another prescribed label or a nonzero degree vector the relevant set is empty. A fixed index-one triangle or universal index-minus-one triangle cannot occur. A matching one-parameter family is exactly its compact parameter interval, with its two identical endpoint counts; there are no nonconstant strips, spheres or boundary disks. Thus its differential is zero and its triangle and parameter-boundary identities hold directly. No strip translation is divided out and no empty tuple is claimed to supply a constituent surface point.

Now suppose that $m>0$ and apply [F1] with the marked points and one witness in every original region protected. The resulting representative has no triple torus intersection and has the same followed pair generators. [F2]'s actual collar extension carries the compression disks and Morse data, identifies the actual Spin-c lift and capped classes, and preserves every old strict witness coefficient under the swept-annulus lattice isomorphism. Thus the new triple has the same required strict admissibility and Spin-c indexing. Its polygon spaces represent exactly the transported literal continuous classes, not classes modulo a sphere or fundamental-group action. A constant triangle would lie in all three tori, so none occurs. This explicitly permitted auxiliary curve choice is necessary: at a constant triangle the almost-complex parameter derivative vanishes because $du=0$, so no J-only universal argument can be substituted for it.

Apply [F3] to this actual triple and its restricted pair sectors. The geometric strict-domain theorem first supplies a finite lower strip index and finite nonnegative domains in every upper-index band. Its actual auxiliary all-index regular path and bubble budget then produce the open dense good genuine-collar end data with no nonconstant index at most zero and index-one regularity. Hence the ensuing polygon limits have the required regular strip levels; a claim of index-one regularity alone would not justify that conclusion. The source-local Hilbert perturbations give actual fixed-data and one-parameter universal transversality at every nonconstant triangle, preserving the protected divisors, tori and exact product-angle end charts. There are no constant triangles by step1.2.

A triangle has three marked ends and no conformal modulus or translation action. Its fixed count index is therefore $\mu$, and a one-parameter universal count has index $\mu+1$. The domain bounds in [F2] and actual domain-area inequality in [F3] give one energy bound for each required low-dimensional set, across all its literal classes and all nonnegative degree vectors. Every limiting nonconstant strip has positive index. Every nonconstant disk bubble contributes at least two, every sphere at least $2k$, and every regular triangle vertex has nonnegative count dimension. The unconditional determinant index budget of [F3] thus excludes all bubbles in count dimensions zero and one. The only broken one-dimensional ends have one rigid triangle and one rigid strip. The same calculation with the family parameter counted ONCE gives rigid universal index-minus-one triangles and the stated universal index-zero ends. This retains $k=1$ and general intermediate $Y$; it does not borrow a knot-in-$S^3$ disk theorem outside its scope.

The actual product-chart, correction and exhaustion proof in [F3] supplies exactly one collar for every such compatible broken pair. Its global tail estimate promotes compact-core convergence to the true Sobolev chart, so a rigid total set is compact discrete and finite under Countable Choice. Its explicit Hausdorff collar compactification of a one-dimensional space is a compact one-manifold with finite boundary. Degree vectors and the actual total Spin-c structure are carried by each neck smoothing; restricting either these labels or an actual class gives the corresponding open-and-closed part. Thus neither multiple classes with the same domain nor the Spin-c extension orbit creates a missing or an extra end.

Count the boundary of this actual compact one-manifold over $\mathbb F_2$. Writing $F$ for the bilinear triangle count, the strip breaks give $dF+F(d\otimes1)+F(1\otimes d)=0$. The marked vectors add at each actual gluing, so the component weights multiply, with every $w,z$ exponent retained. For a fixed-end one-parameter family its universal one-manifold also has the two parameter endpoints; the universal index-minus-one counts $H$ give $F_1+F_0=dH+H(d\otimes1)+H(1\otimes d)$. These are finite weighted equations, also after specializing every $w$ color to $U$ and every $z$ color to $V$. If the intermediate input $\Theta$ is an actual cycle, substituting it removes the $F(1\otimes d)$ term and gives the required one-input chain map and homotopy. Together with the direct point model in step1.1, this proves exactly the analytic identities; [F4]'s independent top-cycle, elementary-map and movie-invariance duties have not been assumed proved by this calculation.
