Assume AC. Let $M$ be the compact exterior of a smooth fibered knot, equipped with a compatible finite PL structure, and let $G$ be its connected fiber, with nonempty connected boundary. Let $S$ be a connected two-sided properly embedded incompressible finite PL surface. Suppose their boundaries have been aligned, with compatible product collars, and that there is a homeomorphism $h:S\to G$ and a homotopy from the inclusion of $S$ to the inclusion of $G$ composed with $h$, fixed on this aligned boundary through maps into $M$. Then $S$ and $G$ are ambient isotopic relative to $\partial M$. This assertion concerns the actual marked original fiber, not just existence of some fibration with fiber $S$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as an ambient hypothesis; the finite construction and
the ODE interfaces below use no additional choice, so this hypothesis is
dispensable. A smooth manifold with corners here is Hausdorff and second
countable, with charts in relatively open subsets of $[0,\infty)^c\times\mathbb R^{n-c}$
and transition maps smoothly extendible with invertible derivative at corner
points; transitions preserve the local depth and its face germs. Let $M$ be
compact. Then $M$ has a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation.
Corner faces are locally subpolyhedra, and any specified finite union of
closed faces is a subpolyhedron.

If the total boundary already has a finite piecewise smooth triangulation
$f:L\to\partial M$ compatible on all local face intersections, with its
differential fan giving a homeomorphism onto the union of boundary faces of the
tangent orthant at each point, the triangulation extends to $M$, pointwise
preserving $f$ with compatible subdivisions allowed. In the resulting finite
union construction all intersections may be made full subcomplexes. The same
relative conclusion applies to a fixed corner-adapted triangulated closed neighbourhood piece
whose smaller protected subcomplex lies in its relative interior: fitting is
performed away from that protected subcomplex. No extension of arbitrary
incompatible boundary data is asserted.

derivations.claim: Use [F2] to take a neat representative, preserving boundary and incompressibility. Nonseparation is preserved by its ambient topological extension. A short oriented transverse segment through $S$ closes through its connected complement to a loop intersecting $S$ once. Thus the intersection-dual cohomology class of $S$ is primitive. By [F1], $[S]=\pm[F]$ in $H_2(E_K,\partial E_K;\mathbb Z)$. Every loop in $S$ may be represented in its interior and pushed slightly into its two-sided normal product, so its intersection with $S$ is zero. Its value under the fiber's meridian homomorphism is consequently zero. Therefore the inclusion lifts to the infinite cyclic fiber cover $\widetilde E_K=F\times\mathbb R$. The lift is an embedding, since equality of two lifted image points would imply equality of their projected points on the embedded $S$.

Align the finitely many longitude boundary curves by [F3] with distinct fiber-boundary levels in the torus, extending across its collar. In the infinite cyclic cover their lifts are horizontal circles in $\partial F\times\mathbb R$. Straighten the neat surface's smaller boundary collars to the product collars using their simultaneous half-space coordinates, fixed on the boundary curves. The projection of the lifted inclusion is now a proper map $p:(S,\partial S)\to(F,\partial F)$ equal to a product near boundary; every boundary restriction is a diffeomorphism. Its fundamental-group map is injective: the lifted inclusion is injective on fundamental groups by [F2] and covering injection, and $F\times\mathbb R\to F$ is a homotopy equivalence. The relative fundamental class of $F\times\{t\}$ generates $H_2(F\times\mathbb R,\partial F\times\mathbb R)$ and pushes to $[F]$ downstairs. Consequently $[S]=\pm[F]$ from step 1.1 makes the relative degree of $p$ equal to $\pm1$.

Give the compact smooth surfaces the finite triangulations of [F4], choosing matched boundary subdivisions through the actual boundary diffeomorphisms. On their product collars retain the boundary map and its linear collar coordinate; relatively approximate the remaining compact map by a finite PL map. Interior compact separation and sufficiently fine approximation keep it in the target interior, so this is a homotopy of pairs fixed on the original boundary. If $\pi_1S\ne1$, apply the full actual classifier [F4]. Its annular-collapse alternative induces zero on relative $H_2$, contrary to the degree $\pm1$ in step 2.1. Its finite covering alternative has absolute relative degree equal to its number of sheets, by summing the lifted oriented triangles. Thus it has one sheet and is a homeomorphism $h:S\to F$, homotopic to $p$ relative to the aligned boundary. If $\pi_1S=1$, [F5] makes $S$ a disk. Lift $p$ to the cover of $F$ for its trivial image subgroup. An infinite-sheeted cover has relative top homology zero: all coefficients of a finite two-cycle on adjacent oriented triangles agree, and connectedness forces a single coefficient on infinitely many triangles, which must vanish by finite support. A finite-sheeted cover pushes its fundamental class to its sheet number times $[F,\partial F]$. Nonzero degree $\pm1$ therefore forces this cover to have one sheet. Hence $F$ is simply connected and also a disk; its boundary map extends to a disk homeomorphism, homotopic to $p$ relative boundary by convex interpolation in disk coordinates. In either case $S$ has one boundary component. The height coordinate of its lifted inclusion can now separately be homotoped linearly to its one constant boundary height, fixed there. Combine these homotopies in $F\times\mathbb R$ and project to get an actual homotopy of the parametrized inclusion of $S$ to the corresponding fiber, relative to the aligned boundary. This asserts a homotopy of maps, not a projection of an arbitrary embedding isotopy.

The homeomorphism and actual boundary-relative homotopy in step 3.1 meet [F6]. Use [F7] on the pair cut along its transverse smooth surface faces and protected product collars, matching paired face subdivisions before regluing; this gives compatible finite structures retaining the already matched boundary triangulations. That theorem constructs an empty embedded product patch in the actual cut fiber product, verifies that the patch meets only one fiber face so embeds downstairs, and reduces the finite intersection system until the patch is the whole surface. Hence its ambient boundary-relative isotopy carries $S$ to the original marked fiber $F$. Restore the preliminary boundary-torus alignment and neatification if necessary. This proves both the isotopy assertion and its relative aligned-boundary refinement under the authorized AC assumptions.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume countable choice. Let $K:S^1	o S^3$ be a smooth oriented embedding and write its quotient normal bundle as $
u_K=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$. Choose an orientation-preserving trivialization $
u_K\cong S^1	imes\mathbb R^2$ and a tubular map $\Phi:\Omega	o S^3$, meaning a smooth embedding from an open neighbourhood $\Omega\subseteq
u_K$ of the zero section onto an open neighbourhood of $K(S^1)$ with $\Phi(s,0)=K(s)$, such that in these product coordinates $\Omega$ contains $S^1	imes D^2_{2\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$. Here $D^2_r=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:\|z\|\le r\}$ uses the product Euclidean norm induced by the chosen trivialization. Set $N(K)=\Phi(S^1	imes D^2_\epsilon)$, $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, $T_K=\partial E_K$, and let $i:T_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ be inclusion, $p:T_K	o S^1$ the product projection, and $\mu$ the positive boundary of a normal disk, using the normal-plane orientation determined by the orientations of $K$ and $S^3$. A class is primitive if it is not $m$ times another class for any integer $|m|>1$. Then $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ is generated by $[\mu]$. The kernel of $i_*:H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)	o H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is a primitive rank-one direct summand generated by a unique class $[\lambda]$ with $p_*[\lambda]=1\in H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)$. It has a simple closed representative, is the preferred longitude, and $([\mu],[\lambda])$ is a basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free
$R$-modules, and $G$ an $R$-module. Then naturally
$$0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(H_{n-1}C,G)\to H^n\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,G)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_nC,G)\to0$$
is exact.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be a compact $R$-oriented $n$-manifold with boundary $A$, for a commutative unital ring $R$. Cap with its relative fundamental class gives isomorphisms, for every integer $p$,
$$S_p:H^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M,A;R),\qquad T_p:H^p(M,A;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R).$$
Here both maps send a class $a$ to $a\cap[M,A]$ in the displayed target. Empty boundary recovers Poincaré duality. Disconnected and empty manifolds are included. AC is inherited only from the exhaustion and local universal-coefficient arguments in Poincaré duality.

Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable smooth three-manifold, let $F$ be a compact connected smooth subsurface of $\partial M$, and let $N\lhd\pi_1(F)$ be normal. If a continuous disk map into $M$ has its boundary in $\operatorname{Int}F$ with class outside $N$, there is a smoothly properly embedded disk in $M$ whose boundary lies in $\operatorname{Int}F$ and has class outside $N$. No pointwise preservation of the original boundary loop is asserted.

Consequently a compact neatly properly embedded two-sided smooth surface $S$ in such a compact orientable smooth three-manifold is incompressible if and only if its inclusion induces an injection on fundamental groups, component by component. Here incompressibility means absence of a smooth embedded compressing disk, with the conventions of the indicated definition.

Let $M$ be a compact smooth three-manifold, possibly nonorientable and with boundary, and let $f:F\to M$ be a smooth embedding of a compact smooth surface with $f^{-1}(\partial M)=\partial F$. Transversality to $\partial M$ is not assumed. Given an open neighborhood $U$ of $C=f(\partial F)$, there is a jointly smooth map $(x,t)\mapsto f_t(x)$ such that each $f_t$ is an embedding, $f_0=f$, every $f_t$ agrees with $f$ on $\partial F$ and outside $f^{-1}(U)$, and $f_t$ is neatly proper for every $t>0$. Time may instead be reparametrized to be stationary near both endpoints; in that version neatness holds after the initial stationary interval.

There is also a jointly continuous ambient isotopy of homeomorphisms $H_t:M\to M$, starting at the identity, supported in $U$, fixing $\partial M$ pointwise, and satisfying $H_t f=f_t$. The construction makes $H_t$ jointly smooth on $(M\setminus C)\times[0,1]$. If $f$ is already neat, the same $f_t$ alternatively admits a jointly smooth ambient extension fixing $\partial M$. No smooth ambient extension at an original tangency is asserted.

Let $F_0=f(F)$ be a compact two-sided smoothly embedded surface in a compact smooth three-manifold, with $f^{-1}(\partial M)=\partial F$, and let $F_1,H_1$ be its angular neatification from [[lem-compact-smooth-boundary-preimage-surfaces-admit-neat-embedding-isotopies]]. The ambient manifold may be nonorientable. If $F_1$ has a smooth compressing disk or smooth boundary-compressing disk, then $F_0$ has a disk of the same type. Boundary-compressing disks can also be transported in the opposite direction: if $F_0$ has one, then $F_1$ has one. Consequently absence of either kind of smooth disk passes from $F_0$ to $F_1$.

Here the boundary-compressing witness has one boundary arc in the surface and the other in $\partial M$, its interior missing both. The construction allows the broader convention of ordinary smooth disk embeddings with tangential endpoint contact, and also gives smooth corner-disk witnesses with transverse surface arcs when that convention is used. No smooth ambient removal of an original surface tangency is asserted.

An essential smooth embedded circle in the standard torus $T=\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2$ represents a nonzero primitive integral homology class. A finite disjoint family of essential smooth circles can be carried by a jointly smooth ambient isotopy of $T$ to parallel affine circles. Two essential circles with the same primitive unoriented class are smoothly ambient isotopic. The components between disjoint essential circles have smooth annulus parameters, with prescribed product collars on their boundary circles. No choice axiom is assumed.

Likewise two smooth spanning arcs of a parametrized annulus with the same endpoints and relative winding number are smoothly ambient isotopic relative to any collars on which they already agree. When disjoint, they have a smooth disk-strip parameter; disjoint essential circles in a parametrized annulus have smooth annulus-strip parameters. All isotopies may be stationary near their time endpoints.

Assume full AC. Let $A,B$ be compact connected oriented surfaces with supplied finite PL triangulations, let $\pi_1(A)\ne\{1\}$, and let $f:(A,\partial A)\to(B,\partial B)$ be a PL map inducing an injective fundamental-group map. Then $f$ is homotopic as a map of pairs either to a finite-sheeted PL covering $A\to B$, or to a map with image in $\partial B$; in the latter alternative $A$ is an annulus.

If the restriction $f|_{\partial A}$ is a local homeomorphism, the homotopy can be chosen constant on $\partial A$. The alternatives retain all orientation signs and all possible finite covering degrees; no assumption that $A$ or $B$ is closed, hyperbolic, or of negative Euler characteristic is imposed.

Let $K$ be finite, $A\subseteq K$ and $B\subseteq L$ subcomplexes, and $f:(|K|,|A|)\to(|L|,|B|)$ continuous. 1. The assignment $$[p:(E,e_0)\to(B,b_0)]\longmapsto p_*\pi_1(E,e_0)$$ is a bijection from based-isomorphism classes of based connected coverings of $B$ to subgroups of $G$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

There are the following explicit valid finite planar codes, with the standard right/up orientation of the plane and positive based meridians using compatible common upper-collar access paths.

The counterclockwise square with vertices $(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1)$ is a crossing-free unknot code. It has one under-arc and gives $\pi_1(S^3\setminus U)=\langle x\mid\ \rangle\cong\mathbb Z$, with $x$ the positive meridian.

| $r$ | $C_r$ | $rOi$ | $rOo$ | $rUi$ | $rUo$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $1$ | $(-423,0)$ | $(-627,102)$ | $(-363,-30)$ | $(-363,30)$ | $(-627,-102)$ |
| $2$ | $(0,-9)$ | $(-33,-6)$ | $(99,-18)$ | $(-99,-18)$ | $(33,-6)$ |
| $3$ | $(0,9)$ | $(33,6)$ | $(-99,18)$ | $(99,18)$ | $(-33,6)$ |
| $4$ | $(423,0)$ | $(627,-102)$ | $(363,30)$ | $(363,-30)$ | $(627,102)$ |

The complete cyclic visit list is $$1O,\ 2U,\ 3O,\ 1U,\ 4O,\ 3U,\ 2O,\ 4U.$$ For every successive pair $rB,sD$ in this list, including the last-to-first pair, use the three straight segments of the route $C_r\to rBo\to sDi\to C_s$. At each crossing pair $rOi$ with $rOo$, and $rUi$ with $rUo$; the first pair is over. Smooth the degree-two bends in disjoint small disks. The cyclic orders at crossings are the counterclockwise lists $(rOo,rUi,rOi,rUo)$ for $r=1,4$ and $(rOo,rUo,rOi,rUi)$ for $r=2,3$.

diagram in $D^2\times[0,1]$ or a finite regular oriented diagram of a nonempty
labeled closed link. In string-link mode, choose the product-tube parallel to
be the blackboard push-off determined by the projected tangent, carried
through the fixed endpoint collars. Choose one initial strand on each
component. Arbitrary independent access paths and other degree-one parallels remain allowed, with their exact correction formula specified below. Traverse component $K_j$ in its orientation
(from bottom to top for a string link and once around for a closed link). At
each undercrossing $c$ of $K_j$, let $o(c)$ be the over-strand, and set
$\epsilon_c=+1$ if the traversal goes from the source side to the target side
of the over-strand's positive in-plane normal, and $\epsilon_c=-1$ if it goes
from target to source. If the undercrossings in traversal order are
$c_1,\ldots,c_s$, define
$$W_j(D)=x_{o(c_1)}^{\epsilon_{c_1}}\cdots x_{o(c_s)}^{\epsilon_{c_s}}.$$

link, it represents the blackboard parallel in $\pi_1(E_L)$. The preferred
zero-self-meridian longitude in the closed-link case is represented by
$$\lambda_j(D)=x_j^{-\operatorname{wr}_j(D)}W_j(D),$$
where $x_j$ is the initial meridian on $K_j$ and $\operatorname{wr}_j(D)$ is
the sum of crossing signs at self-crossings of $K_j$.

Assume full AC. Let $G$ be finitely presented, let its reduced complex $SL_2$ representation variety have its trace-coordinate affine character quotient, and let $X$ be a nonempty irreducible closed subset of that quotient containing an irreducible character. Write $A=\mathbb C[X]$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. There is a field $L/K$ of degree at most two and an absolutely irreducible representation $\sigma:G\to SL_2(L)$ whose every word trace is the corresponding function on $X$.

More precisely, for some $0\ne f\in A$ there is a subring $B\subset L$ which is either $A_f$ or the free rank-two algebra $A_f[\xi]=A_f[T]/(T^2-aT+1)$, where $a$ is one word trace and $a^2-4$ is a unit. All generator matrices lie in $SL_2(B)$. Every $\chi\in D_X(f)$ admits a homomorphism $B\to\mathbb C$ extending evaluation at $\chi$; every resulting representation has character $\chi$ and is irreducible. This is an actual family of representatives, not merely agreement of formal traces. One can enlarge $f$ to make any specified finite list of nonzero elements of $L$ and their inverses belong to $B$.

If $[L:K]=2$, its nonidentity automorphism $\tau$ acts on $\sigma$ by simultaneous conjugation with an explicit matrix $P\in GL_2(L)$. Consequently any projective point obtained from $\sigma$ by finite field operations that commute with field automorphisms and whose value is invariant under simultaneous $GL_2$ conjugation is defined over $K$. This clause presumes that the construction is actually defined and invariant; it supplies no homological rank, tangent-space or essential-surface assertion.

Assume full AC. Let $(Y,y)$ be a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected based space, and fix an isomorphism
$$\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle\ \cong\ \Gamma=\pi_1(Y,y)$$
from a finite presentation. Let $P$ be its presentation $2$-complex, with its one vertex $p$. Choose based loops in $Y$ representing the specified generators. They extend, after choosing fillings of the finitely many relators, to a based map $f:P\to Y$ inducing the specified isomorphism. No CW structure on $Y$ is required. For every left $\mathbb Z[\Gamma]$-module $A$, interpreted as the base fibre of a local system with $g a=T_{\bar g}a$ in the first-loop-first convention, this map induces an isomorphism
$$H_1(P;f^*\mathcal A)\ \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\ H_1(Y;\mathcal A).$$
This assertion does not require $Y$ or its universal cover to be aspherical and does not assert that $P$ is a spine or a homotopy-equivalent model of $Y$.

There is the following explicit finite-chain form. Give universal-cover chains the right action $c\cdot g=T_{g^{-1}}c$, and choose the lifted presentation vertex $e_0$ and generator edges $e_j$ starting there. For a word $w$ in the generators and their inverses, let each positive letter $x_j$ after prefix $q$ contribute $e_j\cdot q^{-1}$, and each negative letter $x_j^{-1}$ after prefix $q$ contribute $-e_j\cdot(qx_j^{-1})^{-1}$. Denote the sum by $c_w$. Then
$$\partial c_w=e_0\cdot w^{-1}-e_0.$$
If $u\in A$ is fixed by $w$, the tensor $c_w\otimes u$ is a cycle. Under the displayed isomorphism its class is the class of the actual based loop in $Y$ represented by $w$, with initial coefficient $u$; it is independent of the word representative and the relator fillings of $f$.

In particular let $j:(T^2,*)\to(Y,y)$ be a based torus map with ordered based loops $(\lambda,\mu)$, choose words $w_\lambda,w_\mu$ for their images, and let $u$ be fixed by both. The two finite cycles $c_{w_\lambda}\otimes u,c_{w_\mu}\otimes u$ compute the images of the actual torus classes in precisely this order. If $A$ is a finite-dimensional vector space over a field $F$, the presentation complex gives finite matrices $B:C_2\to C_1$, $C:C_1\to C_0$ and these two cycle columns $U$, with $CB=CU=0$. The actual kernel of the two peripheral classes mapping into $H_1(Y;\mathcal A)$ is exactly
$$\ker\{F^2\xrightarrow{U}\ker C/\operatorname{im}B\}.$$
Thus a one-dimensional image of those two actual peripheral classes is equivalent to $\operatorname{rank}_F(B\mid U)=\operatorname{rank}_FB+1$. All matrix entries are finite sums of matrices for generator words and their inverses. For the left coefficient action $\operatorname{Ad}\rho$ of an $SL_2$ representation they are polynomial in the representation entries and in the chosen vector $u$. For a torus restriction with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\mu))^2\ne4$, one may take $u=\rho(\mu)-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\mu))I$ in characteristic different from $2$; the two torus classes are then a basis. This applies, in particular, to an actual compact smooth knot exterior and its based peripheral torus map. No existence of a generic representation family or generic exterior rank is inferred.

Let $F$ be a field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $L,M\in SL_2(F)$ commute. Write $t=\operatorname{tr}M$ and suppose $\Delta=t^2-4\ne0$. Give the torus $T^2$ an ordered pair of based oriented generating loops $(\lambda,\mu)$, and give its adjoint local system intrinsic monodromies $P=\operatorname{Ad}L$ and $Q=\operatorname{Ad}M$ on $V=\mathfrak{sl}_2(F)$. Here monodromy acts on column coefficient vectors on the left. Set
$$v=M-\frac t2 I,\qquad W=\{X\in V:\operatorname{tr}(vX)=0\}.$$
Then $V=Fv\oplus W$, both summands are preserved by $P,Q$, and $P,Q$ are the identity on $Fv$. There is an explicit split chain model
$$0\longrightarrow V\xrightarrow{d_2}V\oplus V\xrightarrow{d_1}V\longrightarrow0,$$
where $d_2z=((I-Q)z,(P-I)z)$ and $d_1(x,y)=(P-I)x+(Q-I)y$, in the ordered edge coordinates $(\lambda,\mu)$. Its $W$ subcomplex is contractible, so
$$H_0(T^2;V)=F[v],\qquad H_1(T^2;V)=F[v\otimes\lambda]\oplus F[v\otimes\mu],\qquad H_2(T^2;V)=F[v\otimes[T^2]].$$

Thus the slope is conjugation invariant wherever its given admissible definition applies. Choose one such loop $\delta$. If $\delta$ is the longitude, apply [F3] with the two torus generators interchanged and then restore the ordered (longitude,meridian) coordinates. In either case $u=\rho(\delta)-\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\delta))I/2$ is nonzero and its two named classes are an actual basis. Apply [F1] to obtain $\sigma$ over $L$, with $[L:K]\le2$, and its spreading ring $B$ over a principal localization of $A$. The proof of [F1] also gives a nonempty open irreducible-character certificate on $X$. Intersect it with the supplied dense admissible open; this is nonempty because $X$ is irreducible. citations.quote: Assume full AC and let $G=\pi_1(E_K)=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle$ be a finite presentation of a knot-exterior group. The set of homomorphisms $G\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ is the affine algebraic subset of $SL_2(\mathbb C)^n$ cut out by the matrix-entry equations $r_j(A_1,\ldots,A_n)=I_2$ for $1\le j\le m$. After each inverse letter is replaced by the adjugate of its determinant-one matrix, these equations have integer coefficients in the matrix-entry coordinates.

Assume full AC. Let $G=\pi_1(E_K)$ be the group of a smooth oriented knot exterior, with positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$. For a finite presentation $G=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle$, the **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$ representation variety** is the algebraic set of tuples $(A_1,\ldots,A_n)\in SL_2(\mathbb C)^n$ for which every relator matrix $r_j(A_1,\ldots,A_n)$ equals the identity. The group $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ acts on this set by simultaneous conjugation. Its affine categorical quotient, whose coordinate ring is the invariant ring of regular functions, is the **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$ character variety** $X(E_K)$. For a representation $\rho$, its character is the function $\gamma\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\gamma))$. A representation is **reducible** if its matrices preserve a common one-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb C^2$; otherwise it is irreducible. The peripheral torus group is $\pi_1(T_K)\cong\mathbb Z^2$, generated by the meridian and preferred longitude; its image in $G$ is generated by their commuting classes and need not be isomorphic to $\mathbb Z^2$. Their image under any representation is a commuting pair of matrices, so it has a common invariant line and is simultaneously triangularizable over $\mathbb C$. Choosing a common invariant line gives meridian and longitude eigenvalues $(M,L)\in(\mathbb C^*)^2$; the unordered boundary character identifies $(M,L)$ with $(M^{-1},L^{-1})$. Simultaneous diagonalizability is stronger than simultaneous triangularizability.

Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the named suppliers. Let $G$ be a
complex reductive affine algebraic group and let $X$ be an affine algebraic set
with an algebraic $G$-action ([[def-rational-action-on-affine-variety]]). Then:
(i) $\mathbb C[X]^G$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb C$-algebra; (ii) for any
finite generating set $f_1,\dots,f_n$ of $\mathbb C[X]^G$ the image of the
morphism $X\to\mathbb C^n$, $x\mapsto(f_1(x),\dots,f_n(x))$, is closed and is
canonically isomorphic to the affine variety with coordinate ring
$\mathbb C[X]^G$, so the quotient is independent of generators up to this
canonical isomorphism; (iii) the resulting surjective $G$-invariant morphism
$\pi:X\to X/\!/G:=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[X]^G$ is a categorical quotient
([[def-categorical-and-geometric-quotients-of-classical-varieties]]); (iv) for
every closed $G$-stable subset $Y\subseteq X$ the induced morphism
$Y/\!/G\to X/\!/G$ is a closed immersion, and for closed $G$-stable
$Y,Y'\subseteq X$ one has $\pi(Y\cap Y')=\pi(Y)\cap\pi(Y')$; (v) every fibre of
$\pi$ contains exactly one closed $G$-orbit; (vi) if $X$ is irreducible then so
is $X/\!/G$, and if in addition $X$ is normal then so is $X/\!/G$.

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with exterior $E_K$, positive meridian $\mu$, and preferred longitude $\lambda$. Define $\mathcal E_K\subset(\mathbb C^*)^2$ to consist of all pairs $(M,L)$ for which some representation $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ has a common invariant line on which $\rho(\mu)$ acts by $M$ and $\rho(\lambda)$ acts by $L$. The Zariski closure is the smallest Zariski-closed algebraic subset containing $\mathcal E_K$; let $V_K$ be the union of its one-dimensional irreducible components, where an irreducible component is a maximal irreducible closed subset. Zero-dimensional image components are omitted. The **ordinary A-polynomial** $A_K(M,L)$ is the Laurent polynomial generating the vanishing ideal of $V_K$, chosen square-free (no repeated irreducible factors) and with primitive integer coefficients (their greatest common divisor is one). It is determined up to multiplication by $\pm M^aL^b$ for $a,b\in\mathbb Z$. Its reduced curve includes the abelian component $L=1$; equivalently, its representative in $\mathbb Z[M,L]$ is divisible by $L-1$.

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot. The restriction of representations of $\pi_1(E_K)$ to the peripheral torus gives an algebraic eigenvalue locus in $(\mathbb C^*)^2$. Its one-dimensional reduced image components are exactly the curve components used in $A_K(M,L)$; isolated image points contribute no curve factor. Eliminating the representation and trace coordinates from the finite presentation equations yields the Laurent ideal of that curve union, whose square-free primitive generator is $A_K$ up to $\pm M^aL^b$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented $3$-sphere, let $N(K)$ be a chosen closed tubular solid-torus neighborhood, let $E_K=\overline{S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)}$, and let $T_K=\partial E_K=\partial N(K)$. Let $\mu$ be the positive oriented meridian, meaning the boundary of a positive normal disk in $N(K)$, and let $\lambda$ be a preferred longitude, meaning a degree-one parallel of the core $K$ in $N(K)$ that is null-homologous in $E_K$. Assume that $[\mu],[\lambda]$ are an ordered basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$, with the boundary-orientation convention $\mu\cdot\lambda=-1$. A slope is the unoriented isotopy class of an essential simple closed curve on $T_K$ whose homology class is $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ for coprime integers $p,q$ not both zero; $(p,q)$ and $(-p,-q)$ represent the same slope. For a slope represented by $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$, the Dehn filling $E_K(p/q)$ is obtained by gluing an oriented solid torus $D^2\times S^1$ to $E_K$ by an orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphism that sends $[\partial D^2\times\{1\}]$ to that slope; the filled orientation agrees with the fixed orientation on $E_K$. If $q\ne0$, the coefficient is written $p/q$; the meridional slope is $1/0$, and integer $n$-framed filling means slope $n[\mu]+[\lambda]$. The oriented homeomorphism type is independent of the gluing map once its meridian image is fixed.

Let $X=U\cup V$, where $U$ and $V$ are open path-connected subsets of $X$, let $U\cap V$ be path-connected, and fix $x_0\in U\cap V$. For the inclusion-induced maps in the diagram

$$\pi_1(U,x_0)\longleftarrow\pi_1(U\cap V,x_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(V,x_0),$$

the group $\pi_1(X,x_0)$, together with the two inclusion-induced homomorphisms, is a pushout ([[def-pushout-of-group-homomorphisms]]). Equivalently, the canonical homomorphism from any pushout $P$ of the displayed diagram to $\pi_1(X,x_0)$ is an isomorphism. No injectivity of either map from the overlap group is assumed.

For homomorphisms $f:K\to G$ and $h:K\to H$, let $N$ be the normal closure in $G\ast H$ of $$\{j_G(f(k))j_H(h(k))^{-1}:k\in K\}.$$ Then $(G\ast H)/N$, with the induced factor maps $j_G$ and $j_H$, is a pushout of $f$ and $h$.

Let $A\subseteq X$, let $i:A\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion, and choose $a\in A$. If $A$ is a retract of $X$ ([[def-retraction-and-deformation-retract]]), then

$$i_*:\pi_1(A,a)\longrightarrow\pi_1(X,a)$$

is injective. If $A$ is a deformation retract of $X$, the inclusion and retraction induce mutually inverse fundamental-group isomorphisms at every basepoint of $A$.

$\operatorname{Deg}:\pi_1(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z,[0])\to(\mathbb Z,+)$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse is

$$n\longmapsto[\omega_n].$$

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar.

A smooth collar is a smooth embedding $c:\partial M\times[0,\varepsilon)\to M$ such that $c(p,0)=p$ and whose image is an open neighbourhood of $\partial M$ in $M$. Locally one may first use a positive smooth width depending on $p$.

derivations.claim: Inclusion of the boundary torus into the exterior gives a homomorphism of fundamental groups. Precomposing a representation with this homomorphism is polynomial in matrix entries, so it is a regular map of representation varieties and is equivariant for simultaneous conjugation.

Pullback along this equivariant map sends conjugation-invariant regular functions to conjugation-invariant regular functions, hence induces the algebraic restriction morphism on affine categorical quotients.

By [F2], the defining equation of the reduced curve union vanishes on each of its one-dimensional image components. The definition takes only those components, so an isolated image point outside their union is not added as a curve factor.

Write the attached solid torus as $V=D^2\times S^1$, let $A=\{0\}\times S^1$, and base at $(0,1)$. The retraction $r(z,w)=(0,w)$ and inclusion $i:A\hookrightarrow V$ satisfy $r\circ i=\operatorname{id}_A$, and the homotopy $((z,w),t)\mapsto((1-t)z,w)$ from $\operatorname{id}_V$ to $i\circ r$ fixes the basepoint. By [F5] and [F6], $\pi_1(V,(0,1))\cong\pi_1(S^1,1)\cong\mathbb Z$.

By [A1] and [F7], the exterior boundary has a collar; $V$ has its product collar. Thickening the two pieces across opposite halves of the gluing collar gives an open cover of the filled manifold whose sets retract to $E_K$ and $V$ and whose intersection retracts to the torus. These spaces are path connected, so [F4] identifies the filled fundamental group as their pushout.

Since $\mu,\lambda$ commute, the primitive class $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ is represented by $\mu^p\lambda^q$. It maps to the identity in $\pi_1(V)$ because it is the meridian. Complete $(p,q)$ to a unimodular basis of $\mathbb Z^2$ by Bézout; the complementary class has longitude coefficient $\pm1$ on $\partial V$, hence maps to a generator of $\pi_1(V)$ by step 2.1. The pushout from step 2.2 identifies this generator with the image of the complementary class in $\pi_1(E_K)$ and imposes only the relation $\mu^p\lambda^q=1$. Eliminating the generator gives $\pi_1(E_K(p/q))\cong\pi_1(E_K)/\langle\!\langle\mu^p\lambda^q\rangle\!\rangle$.

A homomorphism from this quotient is exactly a homomorphism from $\pi_1(E_K)$ that kills $\mu^p\lambda^q$. Since $\rho(\mu)$ and $\rho(\lambda)$ commute, this condition is the matrix equation $\rho(\mu)^p\rho(\lambda)^q=I_2$.

If the two peripheral matrices are simultaneously diagonalized, their product of powers is $\operatorname{diag}(M^pL^q,(M^pL^q)^{-1})$, which is the identity exactly when $M^pL^q=1$. For a merely triangular pair, the diagonal entries still give this necessary equation, but they do not determine the off-diagonal entries of the product; the matrix relation remains the exact test.

**The exact instanton interface selects a nonvertical path.** Under [L1], its first alternative makes $\mathcal S(K)$ empty: for any finite $p/q$ choose $\beta=-p\pi/(2q)$ modulo $2\pi$ on that full vertical circle, giving an actual irreducible filling representation. Hence an SU2-averse knot, for which $\mathcal S(K)$ is infinite, must satisfy the second alternative. On a smaller closed subinterval its meridian is noncentral and already diagonal. Its commuting longitude is diagonal too; its eigenvalue is a continuous circle-valued function, so subdivision into finitely many open semicircle charts gives a continuous real lift $\beta$. The meridian coordinate $\alpha=s$ has distinct endpoint values. This is the ONLY use of [L1] in steps3.1–7.1; no bare nontrivial-knot representation-existence assertion is silently substituted for its varying-meridian conclusion.

Step1.1 gives $|p/q-r_0|<C/q\le C$ for EVERY $p/q\in\mathcal S(K)$. Thus the full set is contained in the fixed bounded interval $[r_0-C,r_0+C]$; an unbounded exceptional subsequence is excluded. In a bounded interval there are only finitely many reduced fractions with denominator at most any fixed $Q$: for each $1\le q\le Q$ only finitely many integers $p$ satisfy the interval bound. Consequently, along EVERY sequence of pairwise distinct elements of $\mathcal S(K)$, $q\to\infty$ and the displayed inequality forces $p/q\to r_0$. The infinite set therefore has exactly one accumulation point in $\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$, namely the finite $r_0$. This proves both quantifiers needed when passing to arbitrary infinite subsets.

**All lifted paths are straight and parallel.** Apply step1.1 to any two points of any continuous lifted irreducible peripheral path and to a sequence of distinct elements of the FULL set. Divide by $q$ and use step3.1 to obtain $r_0(\alpha_1-\alpha_0)+(\beta_1-\beta_0)=0.$ Thus $\beta+r_0\alpha$ is constant on each path, and any nonconstant one lies on a line of slope $-r_0$. No finite-component or semialgebraic path-selection assertion is required for this implication.

**A nonzero Laurent equation actually vanishes on this arc.** For completeness the needed image-dimension operation is the accepted field-linear adjoint calculation [F2], not an assumption that the A-polynomial Definition excludes larger images. If a generic irreducible eigenline-incidence component had algebraically independent $M,L$, its function field would admit two derivations independently differentiating $M,L$; extend these through its finite separable algebraic part by the minimal-polynomial derivative formula. The actual boundary homology has dimension two. Self-duality and the pair exact sequence make both boundary inclusion and cohomological restriction rank one. The actual word/eigenbasis pairing therefore puts ALL logarithmic derivative pairs $(DL/L,DM/M)$ in the same line, contradicting those two independent derivations. Reducible components have $L=1$ by knot abelianization. All peripheral images thus have dimension at most one. The finitely many zero-dimensional image components give only finitely many points. The nonconstant interval of step4.1, after discarding these points, lies in the union of the one-dimensional image curves; hence the nonzero Laurent polynomial $A_K$ in [F3] vanishes on it. By continuity it vanishes on the entire interval. This argument allows arbitrary dimensions of the underlying character components and does not confuse a one-parameter family with a maximal image component.

**Rationality by a finite exponential calculation.** Write $A_K(M,L)=\sum_{(a,b)\in T}c_{ab}M^aL^b$, with finite distinct integral pairs and nonzero coefficients. On the interval $M=e^{i\alpha}$, $L=e^{i(c-r_0\alpha)}$, step5.1 gives $\sum_{(a,b)\in T} c_{ab}e^{ibc}e^{i(a-r_0b)\alpha}=0.$ If $r_0$ were irrational, all real numbers $a-r_0b$ would be distinct: equality for different pairs would either force identical pairs or express $r_0$ as a ratio of integers. Differentiate this finite identity $0,1,\ldots,|T|-1$ times at an interior point. Its coefficient matrix is a Vandermonde matrix in the distinct numbers $i(a-r_0b)$, multiplied by nonzero diagonal exponentials. Its determinant is nonzero, forcing every $c_{ab}e^{ibc}=0$, contrary to their choice. Thus $r_0\in\mathbb Q$. **Full package with explicit external inputs.** Steps1.1–6.1 prove the elementary full-set boundedness, uniqueness and rationality operation from [L1]. The actual alternative is now supplied externally by [L1], while [L2] supplies the additional nonzero bound, L-space surgery, fiberedness, Alexander and satellite interfaces. The accepted filling and closed-lift operations [F4], together with the external knot-exterior trichotomy in [L2], give the geometric reductions required in §§3–5. These establish all four parts of the original package under its stated hypotheses. This completion uses external gauge and classification results; it does not assert local reconstructions of those results.

Reducible components have $L=1$ by knot abelianization. All peripheral images thus have dimension at most one. The finitely many zero-dimensional image components give only finitely many points. The nonconstant interval of step4.1, after discarding these points, lies in the union of the one-dimensional image curves; hence the nonzero Laurent polynomial $A_K$ in [F3] vanishes on it. By continuity it vanishes on the entire interval. This argument allows arbitrary dimensions of the underlying character components and does not confuse a one-parameter family with a maximal image component.

**Rationality by a finite exponential calculation.** Write $A_K(M,L)=\sum_{(a,b)\in T}c_{ab}M^aL^b$, with finite distinct integral pairs and nonzero coefficients. On the interval $M=e^{i\alpha}$, $L=e^{i(c-r_0\alpha)}$, step5.1 gives $\sum_{(a,b)\in T} c_{ab}e^{ibc}e^{i(a-r_0b)\alpha}=0.$ If $r_0$ were irrational, all real numbers $a-r_0b$ would be distinct: equality for different pairs would either force identical pairs or express $r_0$ as a ratio of integers. Differentiate this finite identity $0,1,\ldots,|T|-1$ times at an interior point. Its coefficient matrix is a Vandermonde matrix in the distinct numbers $i(a-r_0b)$, multiplied by nonzero diagonal exponentials. Its determinant is nonzero, forcing every $c_{ab}e^{ibc}=0$, contrary to their choice. Thus $r_0\in\mathbb Q$. This proves rationality without importing a transcendence-number theorem or claiming arithmetic algebraicity of isolated pillowcase points.

**Full package with explicit external inputs.** Steps1.1–6.1 prove the elementary full-set boundedness, uniqueness and rationality operation from [L1]. The actual alternative is now supplied externally by [L1], while [L2] supplies the additional nonzero bound, L-space surgery, fiberedness, Alexander and satellite interfaces. The accepted filling and closed-lift operations [F4], together with the external knot-exterior trichotomy in [L2], give the geometric reductions required in §§3–5. These establish all four parts of the original package under its stated hypotheses. This completion uses external gauge and classification results; it does not assert local reconstructions of those results.

citations.quote:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers, let $K=T(p,q)$ be the oriented primitive slope curve in the standard Heegaard torus, and let $\rho_t(z_1,z_2)=(e^{2\pi i p t}z_1,e^{2\pi i q t}z_2)$ be the weighted circle action on the unit $S^3\subset\mathbb C^2$. Choose $N(K)$ to be a sufficiently small closed metric tube around the orbit $K$ for the round metric; this tube is invariant because $\rho_t$ is isometric and preserves $K$. Set $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$. Let $x$ and $y$ be based generators of the fundamental groups of the two solid-torus pieces obtained by cutting $E_K$ along the annulus left on the Heegaard torus, oriented so that the annulus core maps to $x^p$ and $y^q$. Then

$$\pi_1(E_K)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle.$$

The common element $h=x^p=y^q$ is central and represents a regular fiber of a Seifert fibration of $E_K$ over a disk. The fibration has two distinguished core fibers of multiplicities $|p|$ and $|q|$; a fiber of multiplicity one is regular, and a fiber of multiplicity greater than one is exceptional. Thus there are exactly two exceptional fibers when $|p|,|q|>1$, and one is regular when one absolute parameter is $1$.

For any integers $\alpha,\beta$ with $p\alpha+q\beta=1$, compatible based paths identify the positive normal-disk meridian and preferred longitude in the peripheral system as

$$\mu=y^\alpha x^\beta,\qquad \lambda=h\mu^{-pq}.$$

Here the positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, and the preferred longitude has degree one around $K$ and maps to zero in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$. Their homology classes form a basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\mathbb Z)$, so both classes are primitive.

Assume full AC. Let $P\subset V=S^1\times D^2$ be an oriented smooth pattern of signed winding $w$, let $C\subset S^3$ be an oriented smooth companion, and form $K=P(C)$ by the specified zero-framed oriented tubular embedding. Let $P(U)$ denote its closure under the zero-framed unknotted embedding of the same product solid torus. Write $X_P=V\setminus\operatorname{int}N(P)$, with outer product marking $(\mu_V,\lambda_V)$. On its inner torus use $(\mu_P,\lambda_P)$, where $\lambda_P$ is the preferred longitude of $P(U)$. Then
$$H_1(X_P;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu_P]\oplus\mathbb Z[\lambda_V],\qquad [\mu_V]=w[\mu_P],\qquad [\lambda_P]=w[\lambda_V].$$
The inner marking becomes exactly the preferred marking $(\mu_K,\lambda_K)$ after satellite gluing. Compatible access paths are retained; arbitrary changes conjugate the corresponding group restrictions and do not change these homology or eigenvalue assertions.

Every irreducible representation of $\pi_1(E_{P(U)})$ extends, after restriction to $X_P$, to an irreducible representation of $\pi_1(E_K)$ with the identical inner peripheral eigenvalues. For $w\ne0$, every one-dimensional irreducible-character peripheral image curve of $C$ has a finite function-field cover carrying an actual irreducible satellite representation whose eigenvalues satisfy
$$M_K^w=M_C,\qquad L_K=L_C^w.$$
Here the common peripheral eigenline is part of the data. No pointwise simultaneous diagonalization at parabolic exceptional points is asserted.

In particular, suppose the enhanced polynomial of $K$ has support on a line of primitive direction $(q,p)$, where the exponent pair $(a,b)$ denotes $L^aM^b$. Then the enhanced polynomial of $P(U)$ has support on a line of the same direction. If $w\ne0$, the enhanced polynomial of $C$ has support on a line of direction $(q w^2,p)$, reduced to a primitive vector when necessary. Unit enhanced polynomials, with one-point support, are included. Thus for a finite slope $r=p/q$, $q\ne0$, pattern closure is $r$-thin and companion is $(r/w^2)$-thin. No assertion that $w\ne0$, that $P(U)$ is nontrivial, or that any knot is fibered or an instanton L-space knot is made here.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1	o S^3$ be a smooth oriented embedding and write its quotient normal bundle as $
u_K=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$. Choose an orientation-preserving trivialization $
u_K\cong S^1	imes\mathbb R^2$ and a tubular map $\Phi:\Omega	o S^3$, meaning a smooth embedding from an open neighbourhood $\Omega\subseteq
u_K$ of the zero section onto an open neighbourhood of $K(S^1)$ with $\Phi(s,0)=K(s)$, such that in these product coordinates $\Omega$ contains $S^1	imes D^2_{2\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$. Here $D^2_r=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:\|z\|\le r\}$. Set $N(K)=\Phi(S^1	imes D^2_\epsilon)$, $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, $T_K=\partial E_K$, and let $i:T_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ be inclusion, $p:T_K	o S^1$ the product projection, and $\mu$ the positive boundary of a normal disk, using the normal-plane orientation determined by the orientations of $K$ and $S^3$. A class is primitive if it is not $m$ times another class for any integer $|m|>1$. Then $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ is generated by $[\mu]$. The kernel of $i_*:H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)	o H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is a primitive rank-one direct summand generated by a unique class $[\lambda]$ with $p_*[\lambda]=1\in H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)$. It has a simple closed representative, is the preferred longitude, and $([\mu],[\lambda])$ is a basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$.

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $p,q\in\mathbb Z$ be coprime and not both zero, and let $E_K(p/q)$ be the Dehn filling whose attached solid-torus meridian is identified with $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$. A closed 3-manifold $Y$ is **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian** if every homomorphism $\pi_1(Y)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ has abelian image. The slope $p/q$ is an **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian surgery slope** for $K$ if $E_K(p/q)$ is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian. The knot admits infinitely many such surgeries if infinitely many distinct rational slopes have this property.

Assume full AC. Let $K=P(C)$ be a zero-framed oriented satellite, with signed pattern winding $w$, and let $P(U)$ be its zero-framed pattern closure. If a slope $p/q$ is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian for $K$, it is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian for $P(U)$.

If $w\ne0$, $\gcd(p,q)=1$ and $q>0$, put $d=\gcd(q,w^2)$. If the primitive satellite filling of slope
$$\frac{p w^2/d}{q/d}=w^2\frac pq$$
is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian, then the companion filling of slope $p/q$ is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian. The meridional case $q=0$ also holds, since both meridional filling groups are trivial. This is an assertion about ALL representations, including reducible nonabelian ones, not merely irreducible characters. Consequently infinitely many distinct rational $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian satellite slopes give infinitely many such slopes for the pattern closure and, when $w\ne0$, for the companion after division by $w^2$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold with $k\ge1$ torus cusps and a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric. Choose an ordered peripheral basis on each cusp. For cusp $i$, let the generalized filling parameter sphere be $S_i=\mathbb R^2\cup\{\infty\}$, with $\infty$ denoting the complete cusp and primitive integral pairs modulo sign denoting ordinary slopes. There is a neighborhood $U$ of $(\infty,\ldots,\infty)$ in $\prod_{i=1}^k S_i$ such that every tuple in $U$ whose finite coordinates are primitive integral slopes determines a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the corresponding ordinary Dehn filling; coordinates equal to $\infty$ remain unfilled complete cusps. Consequently, one may choose neighborhoods $U_i$ of $\infty$ with $\prod_i U_i\subseteq U$, and only finitely many primitive integral pairs at each cusp lie outside $U_i$. Thus every simultaneous filling whose slopes all lie in their respective $U_i$ is hyperbolic. Nonprimitive ray parameters may describe cone or orbifold completions but are not ordinary smooth fillings. No universal numeric length threshold or universal bound on the number of exceptional slopes is asserted.

Assume AC. Every nonempty connected oriented complete Riemannian three-manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$ is isometric to $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$ for a discrete torsion-free subgroup $\Gamma\le\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$. The covering is a universal Riemannian covering and identifies $\Gamma$ with the fundamental group up to the usual basepoint conjugacies. Its completeness and quotient presentation are conclusions from the stated metric hypotheses. The orientation-preserving isometry group of the model is $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$ with its usual Möbius boundary action.

Assume full AC. Let $Y$ be a nonempty closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold equipped with a complete Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$. Its faithful discrete holonomy
$$\rho:\pi_1(Y)\longrightarrow PSL_2(\mathbb C)$$
admits a homomorphism lift $\widetilde\rho:\pi_1(Y)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ through the quotient by $\{I,-I\}$. The lift is faithful. The required Spin structure on $TY$ is actually constructed from a finite complete Heegaard splitting, rather than assumed from the vanishing of a knot exterior's second cohomology.
If $p:E\to B$ is a finite-sheeted covering, then $E$ is compact if and only if $B$ is compact.

Assume full AC. Let a smooth fibered satellite knot be written $K=P(C)$ with essential companion torus $T$, nontrivial companion $C$, and pattern not isotopic to the core of its solid torus. Let $w$ be its signed winding number. Then $w\ne0$ and
$$g(K)=g(P(U))+|w|g(C).$$
More precisely, a product decomposition obtained by cutting the given fiber produces connected-surface mapping-torus descriptions of the companion and pattern-closure exteriors, with fiber surfaces of their minimal Seifert genera. If the symmetric Alexander polynomial of $K$ has nonzero coefficients in both its highest degree and the immediately next degree, then $P(U)$ is nontrivial. No instanton theorem is assumed or proved by this assertion.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in $S^3$, its Seifert genus is zero if and only if $K$ is ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the standard unknot.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary orientation equal to that of $K$, let $g$ satisfy $\chi(F)=1-2g$, and choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Use the positive normal convention $(n,u,v)>0$ and define $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $A_K=H_1(\widetilde X_K;\mathbb Z)$ be the one-variable Alexander module of the knot complement $X_K=S^3\setminus K$, where the cover is classified by the total-linking homomorphism and $t$ acts by the deck transformation corresponding to the positive meridian. Then there is an isomorphism of $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$-modules
$$
A_K\cong\operatorname{coker}\bigl(V-tV^T:\Lambda^{2g}\to\Lambda^{2g}\bigr).
$$

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is $K$, with $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ and use the positive normal convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $A_K$ be the first homology of the infinite cyclic cover of $S^3\setminus K$ classified by total linking, with $t$ acting by the positive-meridian deck transformation. Let $\Delta_K(t)$ be the generator of the zeroth elementary ideal $E_0(A_K)$ in $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, and write $p\doteq q$ when $p$ and $q$ differ by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\Lambda$. Then for every such $F$ and basis,

$$\det(V-tV^T)\doteq\Delta_K(t).$$

The determinant is $1$ for the empty $0\times0$ matrix when $g=0$. This formula concerns the polynomial $\Delta_K$; the existing knot-normalized fraction $D_K=\Delta_K/(1-t)$ is a separate invariant.

For an open cover $X=U\cup V$, the sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(U\cap V;G)\to H_n(U;G)\oplus H_n(V;G)\to H_n(X;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(U\cap V;G)\to\cdots$$
is exact, with middle map $(u,v)\mapsto u+v$.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers, let $K=T(p,q)$, and put $a=|p|$, $b=|q|$. For $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, define
$$\delta_{a,b}(t)=\frac{(t^{ab}-1)(t-1)}{(t^a-1)(t^b-1)}.$$
Then $\delta_{a,b}(t)$ is a polynomial in $\mathbb Z[t]$, the Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$ defined as a generator of the zeroth elementary ideal of the positive-meridian infinite-cyclic-cover module satisfies $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\delta_{a,b}(t)$, and the knot genus is $g(K)=(a-1)(b-1)/2$. Here $f\doteq g$ means $f=\pm t^k g$ for some integer $k$.

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a knot. The input package required by the Baldwin–Sivek thin-knot and infinitely-many-abelian-surgeries arguments consists of the following conclusions with their stated hypotheses: (i) a nontrivial $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-averse knot has a unique rational accumulation slope and either it or its mirror is an instanton L-space knot; (ii) a nontrivial instanton L-space knot is fibered and its symmetrized Alexander polynomial has coefficients in $\{-1,0,1\}$ with nonzero coefficients alternating in sign; (iii) the L-space satellite restrictions and the pattern/companion surgery-transfer statements exclude the satellite cases used in §§3–5; and (iv) the hyperbolic Dehn-filling theorem and the knot-exterior JSJ classification reduce the remaining cases to torus knots. This carrier records the exact imported result interfaces and does not assert that these conclusions have been proved locally.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $E_K$ be the compact connected orientable exterior of a smooth knot in $S^3$, with one torus boundary component. If $E_K$ is irreducible, its boundary is incompressible, $E_K$ is atoroidal, and $E_K$ is not Seifert-fibered, then $\operatorname{int}(E_K)$ admits a complete finite-volume Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$ with one torus cusp. No conclusion is asserted for a torus or satellite knot unless its exterior satisfies all four topological hypotheses.

derivations.claim: **The full torus direction by its actual group.** Let $K=T(a,b)$ with signed coprime nonzero parameters. For every positive integer $n$, the rational slope $(abn+1)/n$ is primitive since $\gcd(abn+1,n)=1$. Its filling relation is $\mu^{abn+1}\lambda^n=\mu h^n=1$ by [F1]. Since $h$ is central, the meridian becomes central. It normally generates, so the entire quotient group is cyclic and EVERY representation has abelian image. The slopes $ab+1/n$ are distinct. This proves the direction for all signed torus knots, including the unit-parameter unknot, without an unproved lens-surgery classification or a restriction to irreducible representations.

**Actual closed lifts exclude the supplied hyperbolic case.** For a primitive rational slope $p/q$ with $p\ne0$, filling abelianization is $\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$: quotient the meridian-generated exterior abelianization by $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]=p[\mu]$. At each all-but-finitely-many hyperbolic filling in [F3], its closed metric has a faithful SL2 lift. An abelian image would make the whole group abelian and hence that finite cyclic group. Its universal cover $\mathbb H^3$ would then be a finite-sheet cover of a closed compact space and so compact, a contradiction. Thus every such nonzero hyperbolic filling has a nonabelian representation. Discarding the single zero slope is harmless. This proves that a supplied finite-volume hyperbolic knot has only finitely many SL2-abelian rational fillings; the closed Spin lift, not the exterior's second cohomology, is essential.

**Filling transfer and the exact conditional limit argument.** Every SL2-abelian filling is SU2-abelian since $SU(2)\subset SL_2(\mathbb C)$. For a nontrivial infinitely-SL2-abelian essential satellite WITH the actual fibered and adjacent-top properties, apply [F4], giving $w\ne0$ and nontrivial pattern closure. In the final reduction these properties are supplied by choosing the actual knot or mirror furnished by [L1] before this row is invoked. Fact [F2] supplies infinitely many actual SL2-abelian slopes for $P(U)$ and $C$, namely $r_i$ and $r_i/w^2$ from distinct satellite slopes $r_i$. Under [L1], the original SU2-abelian slope set is bounded; every infinite subset therefore has a convergent subsequence, and uniqueness of its accumulation point makes its limit $r(K)$. Indeed infinitely many distinct points outside any fixed neighborhood of that point would have a second accumulation point by compactness of a bounded closed interval. Thus the transferred subsets have limits $r(K)$ and $r(K)/w^2$. Applying [L1] to the nontrivial components identifies $r(P(U))=r(K)=w^2r(C)$. No assertion that a mere infinite subset shares a finite accumulation point without boundedness has been used.

**Conditional minimal-genus reduction.** By [L2] and step1.2, a nontrivial infinitely-SL2-abelian nontorus knot would be an essential satellite. Choose such a satellite of least genus. By [L1], one of this knot and its mirror has the actual fibered and specified Alexander properties. Reflection reverses the positive meridian and preserves the degree-one zero-homology longitude by [F1]; the resulting exterior group isomorphism therefore identifies its filling groups with those at negated slopes. It also carries spanning surfaces in both directions, preserving minimal genus, and sends torus knots to torus knots. Replace the least-genus counterexample by that chosen mirror if needed, and choose its essential satellite decomposition by [L2] and step1.2. We now use its ACTUAL supplied fiber and Alexander properties, without an extra assumption on mirror invariance of those coefficients. Thus [F4] and step1.3 give nontrivial $P(U),C$, nonzero $w$, and $g(K)=g(P(U))+|w|g(C)$. Both positive genera are strictly smaller, even for $|w|=1$. Each component has infinitely many SL2-abelian slopes by [F2], so minimality and [L2], with step1.2, make both torus knots. For a signed torus knot the cyclic filling family in step1.1 accumulates at the parameter product; the uniqueness in [L1] identifies its limit slope with that product. Their signed parameter products have the same nonzero sign by step1.3. Let $a>b\ge2$ and $c>d\ge2$ be their respective ABSOLUTE parameter pairs, interchanging parameters when needed. Taking absolute values of that slope relation gives $ab=cdw^2$. The symmetric torus polynomial in [F5] depends only on these absolute parameters, so no further mirroring of the actual satellite and no extra instanton property for either component is needed.

We supply the classical satellite Alexander formula used in [L2], instead of assuming it from a satellite Definition. Write $X=V\setminus\operatorname{Int}\nu P$ for the pattern exterior and $E_K=X\cup_T E_C$ for the satellite exterior, with outer meridian $\mu_V$ identified with $\mu_C$ and preferred outer longitude with $\lambda_C$. Let $w\ne0$ be the winding number, and let $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ act on covers by the satellite's positive-meridian deck transformation. Total linking restricts to $w$ times companion linking on $E_C$, to $w$ on $\mu_V$ and zero on the outer longitude. The pulled-back cover of $T$ has $|w|$ cylinder components, so $H_1(\widetilde T)=\Lambda/(t^w-1)$ generated by a lift of $\lambda_C$; its $H_0$ is the same module. The cover of $E_C$ has $|w|$ components, with module $H_1=\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]}A_C$, where $s$ acts by $t^w$. Its $H_0$ map from $T$ is an isomorphism, because the two linking images are the same subgroup $w\mathbb Z$. Its longitude class is zero in $H_1$: a Seifert surface for $C$ lifts, since linking vanishes on all its loops by normal push-off, and its boundary is that lifted longitude. Replace $C$ by the unknot to obtain the pattern closure $P(U)$. Its companion-side cover has $|w|$ contractible components, the same $H_0$ and zero $H_1$. In both lifted Mayer–Vietoris sequences the $H_0$ map is injective, since its companion-side coordinate is an isomorphism. The only $H_1(\widetilde T)$ image is consequently in the SAME pattern-side module. Quotienting that image yields, respectively, $A_K\cong A_{P(U)}\oplus\bigl(\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]}A_C\bigr)$. All gluings and the chosen longitude bounds are in the actual peripheral marking; no companion character transfer is used in this module calculation.

For $w\ne0$, $\Lambda$ is free of rank $|w|$ over $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$ via $s=t^w$, with basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{|w|-1}$ after reversing the exponent convention if $w<0$. Extension of scalars is therefore exact, and [F5] supplies a square presentation of its companion summand by the companion Seifert matrix with $s$ replaced by $t^w$. The direct sum in step 3.1 has a block-diagonal square presentation. Taking its determinant gives $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\Delta_{P(U)}(t)\Delta_C(t^w)$. With symmetric normalization and value one at $t=1$, the Laurent unit ambiguity disappears. The winding-zero case gives the same polynomial identity with $\Delta_C(1)=1$: its companion-side cover is now a disjoint union of copies of $E_C$, with $H_1=\Lambda[\mu_C]$ and $H_0=\Lambda$. The torus-side groups are $H_1=\Lambda^2$, $H_0=\Lambda$, and the meridian map onto the companion $H_1$ is an isomorphism while the longitude maps to zero. The same maps hold for an unknot companion. Eliminate the companion meridian generator in both sequences; their identical remaining pattern quotient is $A_K\cong A_{P(U)}$. This proves the Alexander satellite formula also for $w=0$, without claiming that such a pattern can be an instanton L-space satellite.

Put $v=|w|$; the symmetric companion polynomial satisfies $\Delta_C(t^w)=\Delta_C(t^v)$. The finite torus-pattern obstruction is also elementary once the stated coefficient restrictions in [L1] have been supplied. Write $a>b\ge2$ coprime and $g=(a-1)(b-1)/2$. The formula in [F5], expanded at infinity, is $\Delta_{T_{a,b}}(t)=t^g(1-t^{-ab})(1-t^{-1})/((1-t^{-a})(1-t^{-b}))$. Modulo terms of degree at most $g-a$, its expansion is $\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor a/b\rfloor}(t^{g-ib}-t^{g-ib-1})$. Thus, for $0\le v<a$, its coefficient $c_{g-v}$ is $1$ if $v=0\pmod b$, $-1$ if $v=1\pmod b$, and zero otherwise. Suppose the companion's normalized polynomial has leading terms $t^h-t^{h-1}+O(t^{h-2})$ and the satellite's nonzero coefficients alternate with absolute value one, exactly the two externally supplied instanton conclusions in [L1]. By step 4.1 its coefficient in degree $g+hv-v$ is $c_{g-v}-1$. If $v=1\pmod b$ this is $-2$, impossible. If $v=qb+r$ with $2\le r<b$, it is $-1$, while the preceding nonzero coefficient is the $-1$ in degree $g+hv-qb-1$: all intervening torus coefficients vanish and no lower companion term reaches those degrees. These consecutive negative coefficients contradict alternation. Consequently $b$ divides $v$ whenever $0<v<a$. This argument is a proved finite polynomial implication and uses the externally supplied instanton properties, without proving their gauge-theoretic foundations.

In particular the torus-pattern configuration required by the minimal-satellite argument is incompatible with those coefficient restrictions. If $ab=k v^2$ for an integer $k\ge1$, then $v<a$, since otherwise $ab\ge a^2>ab$. Step 5.1 makes $b\mid v$, whence $a=k b(v/b)^2$ contradicts $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $b\ge2$. Mirroring a torus pattern does not change its symmetric Alexander polynomial, so the same contradiction applies after the prescribed mirror reduction. Also $v=1$ is already excluded as soon as both nontrivial pattern and companion have leading terms $t^g-t^{g-1}$ and $t^h-t^{h-1}$: their product has second leading coefficient $-2$. This is the finite polynomial contradiction needed for the conditional configuration in step2.1; it does not supply the externally supplied instanton conclusions.

The companion torus in step2.1 has the adjacent leading terms required in step5.1 by its explicit torus formula [F5], without another instanton hypothesis on that companion. With $v=|w|$, the configuration of step2.1 satisfies $ab=cdv^2$; applying step6.1 to this positive $v$ gives a contradiction. Steps1.1–1.2 unconditionally prove the full signed-torus direction and the supplied-metric hyperbolic exclusion; [F2] proves all actual pattern/companion filling cases. Steps1.3–6.1 supply the remaining converse assembly with the exact externally supplied or explicitly conditional premises [L1, L2].
